prefix.description: Only paths starting with this, such as invoices/2026/.

actions.name: Query records
actions.description: The records matching every filter, sorted, as a table (and as a list of dictionaries).

filters.description: Each {field, op, value}; op is =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, contains, starts_with, empty or not_empty. Text compares without case.

table.description: id and every field, one row per record.

actions.name: Update record
actions.description: Change some fields of a record; fields not given keep their values, and an empty value clears a field.

id.description: The record's id.

values.description: Field to new value.

actions.name: Upload file to bucket
actions.description: Put a file from the run's folder into a storage bucket, at a path such as invoices/2026/acme.pdf.

file.description: The file to upload.

path.description: Its path in the bucket (empty: the file's name).

overwrite.description: Replace a file already at that path.

name: Database
description: Connect to databases and run parameterised queries, updates and transactions.

actions.name: Begin transaction
actions.description: Start a transaction; changes are kept only after Commit.

actions.name: Bulk insert
actions.description: Insert every row of a Data Table, or of a delimited text file read line by line, into a database table in batches, all or nothing.

data.description: Data Table whose rows are inserted (or use source_file).

columns.description: Database column for each Data Table or file column, in order; the Data Table's column names (or the file's header) when empty.

batch_size.description: Rows sent to the database per batch.

source_file.description: Delimited text file (CSV) whose rows are inserted instead of a Data Table; it is read as it goes, so large files fit. Empty fields are inserted as NULL.

delimiter.description: Field separator of the file: one character, or tab.

start_row.description: Line of the file where reading starts (1 = the first line); lines above it, such as a title, are skipped.

has_header.description: The first line read holds the column names, used as database columns when columns is empty.

encoding.description: Text encoding of the file, e.g. utf-8 or windows-1252.

column_map.description: G2 (AA parity): source column (Data Table or file header) to database column; columns left out are not inserted.

timeout_seconds.description: G2 (AA parity): cancel a batch the database takes longer than this many seconds over; 0 waits as long as the step allows.

actions.name: Run stored procedure
actions.description: Call a stored procedure or function with input, output and in-out parameters; return the rows it produces, its output values and a function's return value.

parameters.description: Parameters in the procedure's order: a plain value is an input; {"value": v, "direction": "out" or "inout", "type": "varchar|integer|bigint|decimal|double|boolean|date|timestamp", "name": "p_total"} declares an output.

query_timeout_seconds.description: Cancel the statement after this many seconds; 0 waits as long as the step allows.

returns_value.description: Call it as a function ({? = call ...}) and return its value as out_parameters.return.

return_type.description: SQL type of the function's value; varchar when empty.

table.description: First result set, or an empty table.

rows_affected.description: Rows changed, when the database reports it; otherwise -1.

out_parameters.description: Output and in-out values by parameter name (or position 1, 2 ... when unnamed); the function's value as "return".

main.tick: It is a function that returns a value

actions.name: Commit
actions.description: Save the changes made since Begin transaction.

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Open a database connection as a named session.

jdbc_url.description: JDBC URL, e.g. jdbc:sqlserver://host;databaseName=erp; when empty it is built from database_type and the fields below.

database_type.description: Kind of database, used to build the URL when jdbc_url is empty. odbc: any ODBC data source on a Windows runner (a DSN name or an ODBC connection string in database); excel: an Excel workbook through the Excel ODBC driver (sheets are tables, e.g. [Sheet1$]).

port.description: Server port; the database's usual port when empty.

database.description: Database name (service name for Oracle; for odbc a DSN name, or a connection string such as Driver={SQL Server};Server=db01;Trusted_Connection=Yes).

file.description: Database file for SQLite, H2 or Access, or the workbook for excel.

user.description: User name, typed or from the vault.

password.description: Password from the vault.

driver_class.description: JDBC driver class to load first, for drivers that do not register themselves.

login_timeout_seconds.description: Give up connecting after this many seconds; 0 uses the driver's default.

properties.description: Extra driver properties, e.g. {"encrypt": "true"}; Credential values are revealed only to the driver.

read_only.description: Open the connection read-only, so the agent cannot change data by mistake: the database enforces it where it can (PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle), and otherwise OOA refuses statements that change data.

auto_commit.description: Save each statement at once; false starts in a transaction that needs Commit.

instance.description: G2 (AA parity): a named SQL Server instance on the server.

oracle_connect.description: G2 (AA parity): what database names for Oracle: a service name, a SID, or a TNS alias from tnsnames.ora (its folder in properties as oracle.net.tns_admin).

share.description: G2 (AA parity): child agents this one runs may use the connection by its session name.
share.x-ooa-label: Agents this one runs may use it

secrets.description: G2 (AA parity): values from the vault for {{name}} places in jdbc_url, e.g. jdbc:sqlserver://db;password={{pwd}}; never logged.

actions.name: Describe table
actions.description: Return the columns of a table with their types, sizes and whether they accept empty values.

table.description: Columns: name, type, size, nullable, position.

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: Close the session. Uncommitted changes are rolled back.

actions.name: Insert/update/delete
actions.description: Run an INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or DDL statement with ? parameters.

parameters.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order.

query_timeout_seconds.description: Cancel the statement after this many seconds; 0 waits as long as the step allows.

actions.name: Export to CSV file
actions.description: Run a SELECT or a stored procedure with ? parameters and write its rows to a CSV file without loading them into memory.

sql.description: SELECT statement with ? placeholders (or use procedure).

parameters.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order.

delimiter.description: Field separator, e.g. , or ; or tab.

header.description: Write the column names as the first line.

encoding.description: Text encoding of the file.

query_timeout_seconds.description: Cancel the statement after this many seconds; 0 waits as long as the step allows.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file; when false an existing file stops the step.

procedure.description: Stored procedure whose first result set is written, used instead of sql; parameters are its input values in order.

max_rows.description: Stop after writing this many rows; 0 writes them all.

append.description: G2 (AA parity): add the rows to the end of the file when it is there (without a second header line).

skip_when_no_rows.description: G2 (AA parity): make no file when the query gives no rows (path is then empty).

actions.name: List tables
actions.description: List the tables and views the connection can see, optionally in one schema.

schema.description: Only this schema; all schemas when empty.

actions.name: Read from (query)
actions.description: Run a SELECT with ? parameters and return the rows as a table.

parameters.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order.

query_timeout_seconds.description: Cancel the statement after this many seconds; 0 waits as long as the step allows.

actions.name: Roll back
actions.description: Undo the changes made since Begin transaction.

iterators.name: Each row of a SQL query
iterators.description: Run a SELECT with ? parameters and yield each row as a record keyed by column name.

parameters.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order.

query_timeout_seconds.description: Cancel the statement after this many seconds; 0 waits as long as the step allows.

name: Databricks
description: Run SQL on a Databricks SQL warehouse, start and watch jobs, start or stop clusters, and move files in and out of the workspace.

actions.name: Cancel job run
actions.description: Stop a job run that is queued or running.

run_id.description: Run id from Run job now.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

actions.name: Cancel statement
actions.description: Stop a SQL statement that is still running.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Keep the address and sign-in under a session for the steps after it, so they need not repeat them (G6).

workspace_url.description: The workspace url the later steps use (G6).

access_token.description: The access token the later steps use (G6).

session.description: The session's name; the toolkit's default session when empty.

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same session.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

actions.name: Delete file
actions.description: Delete a file from a Unity Catalog volume, the workspace, or DBFS (a DBFS folder with recursive).

remote_path.description: File to delete.

recursive.description: DBFS only: also delete a folder with everything in it.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: Forget the open Databricks session; later steps then need their own address and sign-in (G6).

session.description: The session; the toolkit's default session when empty.

closed.description: True when a session was open.

actions.name: Download file
actions.description: Save a file from a Unity Catalog volume, the workspace, or DBFS to this machine.

remote_path.description: File to download, e.g. /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/file.csv or dbfs:/FileStore/file.csv.

save_as.description: Where to save it on this machine. Missing folders are created.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

overwrite.description: Replace a file already at save_as; when off, the action stops instead and nothing is downloaded. Off for new steps (G6).

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

path.description: Full path of the saved file.

actions.name: Run SQL statement
actions.description: Run SQL on a SQL warehouse and return the rows as a data table. Use :name in the SQL for values passed in parameters.

warehouse_id.description: SQL warehouse that runs the statement: its name or its id (from its Connection details).

parameters.description: Values for :name markers in the SQL, e.g. {"region": "EMEA"}.

catalog.description: Catalog for names that are not fully written out.

schema.description: Schema for names that are not fully written out.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result before returning with status RUNNING.

max_rows.description: Most rows to bring back into the table.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

table.description: Result rows (empty for statements that return no rows).

row_count.description: Number of rows in the table.

statement_id.description: Id of the statement, for status, results or cancel.

status.description: SUCCEEDED, or PENDING / RUNNING when it did not finish within the wait time.

actions.name: Get statement results
actions.description: Read the rows of a finished SQL statement into a data table, chunk by chunk.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for a running statement to finish; 0 fails at once if it is still running.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

row_count.description: Number of rows in the table.

total_rows.description: Rows in the full result, which can be more than max_rows.

actions.name: Get job run
actions.description: Check the progress and outcome of a job run.

run_id.description: Run id from Run job now.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

life_cycle_state.description: Where the run is, e.g. PENDING, RUNNING or TERMINATED.

result_state.description: SUCCESS, FAILED, TIMEDOUT or CANCELED once finished.

run.description: run_id, life_cycle_state, result_state, state_message, run_page_url, start_time, end_time.

actions.name: Get job run output
actions.description: Read what a finished job run produced: the notebook's result, the error and its trace, and the logs, for each task of the run.

run_id.description: Run id from Run job now.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

result.description: The notebook's exit value (dbutils.notebook.exit); for several tasks, the first task's that has one.

error.description: Why the run failed, when it failed.

error_trace.description: The error's stack trace, when there is one.

logs.description: Output of a Python, JAR or spark-submit task (the last 5 MB).

tasks.description: One row per task: task_key, run_id, result_state, result, error, logs.

actions.name: Get statement status
actions.description: Check whether a SQL statement that was left running has finished.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

status.description: PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELED or CLOSED.

message.description: Error text when the statement failed.

total_rows.description: Rows in the result once it succeeded.

actions.name: List clusters
actions.description: Return the workspace's clusters and their state.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

table.description: Columns: cluster_id, name, state, spark_version, node_type, creator.

actions.name: List jobs
actions.description: Return the jobs in the workspace, optionally only those with a given name.

name.description: Only the job with exactly this name.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

actions.name: Run job now
actions.description: Start a job right away, optionally with parameters, and wait for it to finish if you like.

job_id.description: Job to start: its name or id (see List jobs).

wait.description: Wait for the run to end before going on.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds and fail with WAIT_TIMEOUT (the run goes on in Databricks).

fail_if_run_fails.description: When waiting, stop the agent with an error if the run does not succeed.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

life_cycle_state.description: Where the run is, e.g. PENDING, RUNNING or TERMINATED.

result_state.description: SUCCESS, FAILED, TIMEDOUT or CANCELED once it has finished; empty before that.

run_page_url.description: Link to the run in the Databricks workspace.

actions.name: Start cluster
actions.description: Start a stopped cluster, and wait until it is running if you like. Nothing happens if it is already running.

cluster_id.description: Cluster to start: its name or id (see List clusters).

wait.description: Wait until the cluster is ready before going on.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds and fail with WAIT_TIMEOUT.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

state.description: Cluster state afterwards, e.g. PENDING or RUNNING.

actions.name: Stop cluster
actions.description: Stop a running cluster to save cost. Its settings are kept so it can be started again. Optionally wait until it has stopped.

cluster_id.description: Cluster to stop: its name or id.

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

wait.description: Wait until the cluster has stopped before going on.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds and fail with WAIT_TIMEOUT.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

state.description: Cluster state afterwards, e.g. TERMINATING or TERMINATED.

actions.name: Upload file
actions.description: Copy a local file into a Unity Catalog volume, the workspace, or DBFS.

local_path.description: File on this machine to upload.

remote_path.description: Destination, e.g. /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/file.csv or dbfs:/FileStore/file.csv.

overwrite.description: Replace a file that is already there; off for new steps (G6).

access_token.description: Databricks personal access token or OAuth token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of a service principal, to sign in with OAuth instead of a personal access token (G6).

client_secret.description: The service principal's OAuth secret from the vault (G6).

remote_path.description: Where the file was written.

name: Data Table
description: Build, filter, sort, search and change in-memory tables.

actions.name: Add column from list
actions.description: Add a column at the start, the end or a zero-based position, filled with the items of a list row by row; a longer list adds rows.

table.description: Table to add the column to.

list.description: Items for the new column: the first item goes in the first row, and so on. Rows beyond the list stay empty.

position.description: Zero-based column position (0 = first); at the end when empty.

actions.name: Add row
actions.description: Append a row: a Dictionary of column values, or a List of values in column order.

values.description: Column name to value (Dictionary), or the values in column order (List).

actions.name: Group and summarise
actions.description: Group rows by one or more columns and compute count, sum, average, minimum, maximum, first or last per group; without group columns, one summary row.

group_by.description: Columns to group by, e.g. ["Vendor"]; one summary row for the whole table when empty.

summaries.description: New column name to 'function:column', e.g. {"Total": "sum:Amount", "Invoices": "count"}. Functions: count, sum, avg, min, max, first, last, count_distinct.

sort_groups.description: Order the groups by their group values; in order of first appearance when off.

table.description: One row per group: the group columns, then one column per summary.

actions.name: Change column type
actions.description: Convert every value in a column to String, Number, DateTime or Boolean; empty cells stay empty.

column.description: Column to convert.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

date_format.description: Pattern of the text when converting to DateTime, e.g. dd/MM/yyyy, or a ready format: ISO_DATE, ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME, ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME, BASIC_ISO_DATE, RFC_1123_DATE_TIME...; ISO dates when empty.

actions.name: Clear rows
actions.description: Remove every row but keep the columns.

table.description: Empty table with the same columns.

actions.name: Column count
actions.description: Number of columns.

non_empty_only.description: Count only columns with at least one value.

actions.name: Column name
actions.description: Return the name of the column at a zero-based index.

actions.name: Column names
actions.description: List the column names in order.

actions.name: Column to list
actions.description: Return the values of one column as a list, e.g. every invoice number.

column.description: Column name.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

list.description: The column's values, top to bottom.

actions.name: Create empty table
actions.description: Make a table with the columns you name (or a number of columns) and a number of empty rows, ready to fill.

column_count.description: Number of columns, named Column1, Column2 ...

actions.name: Delete column
actions.description: Remove a column and its values.

column.description: Column to remove.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

actions.name: Delete rows
actions.description: Delete the row at a position, or every row where a column equals a value.

column.description: Column to match (used when row is empty).

value.description: Delete rows whose column equals this value.

actions.name: Filter rows
actions.description: Keep (or remove) the rows that meet one or more conditions on their columns, and keep only the columns you need.

column.description: Column name.

operator.description: Comparison; matches takes a regular expression.

value.description: Value to compare with (not needed for empty/not_empty).

match_case.description: Compare text with upper/lower case taken into account.

more_conditions.description: More conditions, each a column, a comparison and a value (column, operator, value, match_case).

match.description: With more conditions: a row must meet all of them, or any one.

keep.description: Keep the rows that meet the conditions, or remove them and keep the rest.

columns.description: Only these columns in the result, in this order; all of them when empty.

actions.name: Find value
actions.description: Return the zero-based numbers of rows containing a value, in one column or in any column.

column.description: Search only this column; all columns when empty.

match.description: equals (numbers compare by value) or contains (text).

match_case.description: Compare text with upper/lower case taken into account.

found.description: True when at least one row matches.

cells.description: Every matching cell as a dictionary with zero-based row and column numbers and the column name.

first_row.description: Zero-based number of the first matching row, or -1.

actions.name: Create from CSV text
actions.description: Build a table from CSV text held in a variable (for example an e-mail body or an API answer), with quoted fields understood.

text.description: CSV text, one row per line.

delimiter.description: One character between fields: , ; | or tab.

header.description: The first line holds the column names; Column1, Column2 … when off.

convert_numbers.description: Store fields that are plain numbers, such as 12.5, as numbers; codes with a leading 0 stay text.

actions.name: Create from records
actions.description: Build a table from a list of dictionaries.

actions.name: Get value
actions.description: Read one cell by zero-based row number and column name.

column.description: Column name.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

actions.name: Insert column
actions.description: Add a column at the end or at a zero-based position, filled with a default value or with the values of a column of another table.

default_value.description: Value for every existing row; empty when not set.

position.description: Zero-based column position; at the end when empty.

source_table.description: Table whose column is copied into the new column, row by row; rows it does not have get the default value.

source_column.description: Name of the column of source_table to copy.

source_column_index.description: Zero-based index of the column of source_table to copy; used when source_column is empty.

column_type.description: Convert the new column's values to this type; kept as they are when empty.

actions.name: Insert row
actions.description: Insert a row, given as a dictionary of column values, at a zero-based position.

row.description: Zero-based position for the new row; at the end when empty.

values.description: Column name to value; missing columns stay empty.

actions.name: Join tables
actions.description: Combine two tables on matching key columns; inner keeps matches only, left keeps every row of the first table.

key_columns.description: Columns present in both tables that must match.

join_type.description: inner keeps matches only; left keeps every row of the first table, right every row of the second, full every row of both.

other_key_columns.description: Key columns of the second table when their names differ, in the same order as key_columns.

table.description: Joined table: first table columns, then the second table's other columns.

actions.name: Look up value
actions.description: Find the first row whose column holds a value and return another column of that row, or a fallback value when no row matches.

column.description: Column that holds the value to look for.

value.description: Numbers compare by value; text by equality.

return_column.description: Column whose value is returned from the matching row.

if_not_found.description: Returned when no row matches; empty when not set.

match_case.description: Compare text with upper/lower case taken into account.

value.description: The value from the return column, or the fallback when nothing matches.

found.description: True when a row matches.

row.description: Zero-based number of the matching row, or -1.

actions.name: Merge tables
actions.description: Stack the rows of several tables; columns are matched by name, using the union of all columns or requiring the same ones.

columns.description: union adds missing columns as empty; same fails when columns differ.

actions.name: Remove duplicate rows
actions.description: Keep the first row for each distinct value of the chosen columns (all columns when empty).

actions.name: Remove empty rows
actions.description: Drop the rows in which every cell is empty (or only spaces).

actions.name: Rename column
actions.description: Give a column a new name; its values stay as they are.

column.description: Current column name.

new_name.description: New column name.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

actions.name: Replace values
actions.description: Replace text in the cells of one column or of every column: inside the cell text, or whole cells only.

replace_with.description: New text; empty removes the text found.

column.description: Only this column; every column when empty.

whole_cell.description: Replace only cells whose whole value is the text, e.g. N/A.

match_case.description: Match upper and lower case exactly.

actions.name: Row count
actions.description: Number of rows.

non_empty_only.description: Count only rows with at least one value; rows whose cells are all empty are skipped.

actions.name: Set value
actions.description: Change one cell.

column.description: Column name.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

actions.name: Sort
actions.description: Sort rows by a column.

column.description: Column name.

column_index.description: Zero-based column index; used when 'column' is empty.

ignore_case.description: Sort text without regard to upper/lower case.

then_by.description: Further column names that order rows with equal values, in the same direction.

actions.name: Sum column
actions.description: Add up the numeric values in a column; empty cells are ignored, and text such as 1,000.50 or $ 12 is read as a number.

column.description: Column name.

if_not_number.description: A cell that is not a number: error stops and names its row; skip leaves it out and counts it in skipped.

locale.description: How numbers written as text use separators, e.g. en-US (1,000.50) or de-DE (1.000,50).

skipped.description: Cells that were not numbers and were left out (if_not_number = skip).

actions.name: Convert to CSV text
actions.description: Turn a table into CSV text in a variable, for an e-mail, an API call or a message, without writing a file.

delimiter.description: One character between fields: , ; | or tab.

header.description: Put the column names on the first line.

actions.name: Convert to HTML table
actions.description: Turn a table into an HTML <table> for an e-mail body or a report; cell text is escaped so it shows as written.

header.description: Put the column names in a header row.

borders.description: Draw thin grey lines around the cells (inline styles, so e-mail programs keep them).

actions.name: Convert to records
actions.description: Turn each row into a dictionary keyed by column name.

actions.name: Write to file
actions.description: Save a table as a CSV file or as a JSON list of records, replacing the file.

path.description: Target file, e.g. output/report.csv; a folder keeps the file there; a temporary file in the run's folder when empty (G2, AA's file variable).

header.description: Write the column names as the first CSV line.

encoding.description: Text encoding, e.g. utf-8, utf-8-bom, ansi (windows-1252), utf-16.

append.description: Add the rows to the end of an existing CSV file (no header is repeated).

row_delimiter.description: Text written after each CSV row instead of the line ending, e.g. | or ;\n (\n, \r and \t are understood).

create_folders.description: Create the file's folder when it does not exist; when off, a missing folder is an error.

path.description: Full path of the written file.

conditions.name: Column count is
conditions.description: Compare the number of columns with a number.

conditions.name: Column contains value
conditions.description: True when any row has this value in the column.

column.description: Column name.

conditions.name: Table has column
conditions.description: True when the table has a column with this name.

column.description: Column name.

conditions.name: Table is empty
conditions.description: True when the table has no rows.

conditions.name: Row count is
conditions.description: Compare the number of rows with a number, e.g. more than 0 rows.

name: Date and time
description: Current time, add, difference, format, time zone conversion and working days with business calendars.

actions.name: Add to date
actions.description: Add (or subtract, with a negative amount) a duration to a date.

amount.description: Amount to add; negative to subtract. Fractions are exact for milliseconds to weeks (1.5 days = 36 hours); months, years and business days take whole numbers.

unit.description: Unit of the amount; business_days skips Saturdays, Sundays and the holidays.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, e.g. ["2026-12-25"].

actions.name: Add working days
actions.description: Move a date by a number of working days, skipping the weekend and holidays of a business calendar; a negative number moves back. The start date itself is not counted (1 from Friday is Monday) and 0 keeps the date. The time of day is kept.

days.description: Working days to add, a whole number; negative to go back.

calendar.description: Name of a holiday calendar in One CommandCenter (its holidays and weekend). Read once per run as the run's user; needs the agent to run from One CommandCenter. Leave empty to give the holidays and weekend here.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, as yyyy-MM-dd, e.g. ["2026-12-25"]. Added to the calendar's dates when a calendar is named too.

weekend.description: Days of the week that are not working days, e.g. SAT,SUN (the default) or FRI,SAT; NONE when every day is a working day. When given with a calendar, it replaces the calendar's weekend.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar date counts; the time of day is kept in this zone.

result.description: The date that many working days later (or earlier).

actions.name: Convert time zone
actions.description: Show a date as the time in another time zone, as text with its offset (2026-11-10T14:30+05:30).

time_zone.description: Time zone to convert to: local (the runner's own), UTC or a name such as Europe/London.

actions.name: Difference between dates
actions.description: Return end minus start in the chosen unit (may be fractional).

unit.description: Result unit; business_days counts working days after start up to and including end.

absolute.description: Return the size of the difference without a minus sign when end is before start.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, e.g. ["2026-12-25"].

actions.name: End of period
actions.description: Return the last second (23:59:59) of the day, week (Sunday), month or year containing a date.

actions.name: Format date
actions.description: Format a date as text in a time zone, using a pattern such as dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm.

pattern.description: Pattern, e.g. dd/MM/yyyy, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, MMM d, yyyy.

time_zone.description: Time zone to show the date in: local (the runner's own), UTC or a name such as Asia/Kolkata.

locale.description: Language for month and day names, e.g. en, de-DE, fr-FR.

standard.description: A predefined ISO or RFC format to use instead of the pattern.

actions.name: Get part of date
actions.description: Return one part of a date, such as the year, month, day of week, week of year or quarter, in a time zone.

part.description: Which part to return; day_of_week is 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday, week_of_year follows ISO 8601.

time_zone.description: Time zone the part is read in: local (the runner's own), UTC or a name such as Asia/Kolkata.

result.description: The part: a Number, or text for day_name and month_name.

actions.name: Is after
actions.description: Check whether the first date is later than the second.

include_time.description: Compare the time of day too; when off only the calendar dates (in time_zone) are compared.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar dates are compared when include_time is off.

result.description: True when the first date is later.

actions.name: Is before
actions.description: Check whether the first date is earlier than the second.

include_time.description: Compare the time of day too; when off only the calendar dates (in time_zone) are compared.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar dates are compared when include_time is off.

result.description: True when the first date is earlier.

actions.name: Is equal
actions.description: Check whether two dates are the same moment.

include_time.description: Compare the time of day too; when off only the calendar dates (in time_zone) are compared.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar dates are compared when include_time is off.

result.description: True when the dates are equal.

actions.name: Is leap year
actions.description: Check whether the year of a date, or a year number, is a leap year.

year.description: Year number; used when no date is given.

actions.name: Is working day
actions.description: Check whether a date is a working day in a business calendar: not on its weekend and not one of its holidays.

calendar.description: Name of a holiday calendar in One CommandCenter (its holidays and weekend). Read once per run as the run's user; needs the agent to run from One CommandCenter. Leave empty to give the holidays and weekend here.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, as yyyy-MM-dd, e.g. ["2026-12-25"]. Added to the calendar's dates when a calendar is named too.

weekend.description: Days of the week that are not working days, e.g. SAT,SUN (the default) or FRI,SAT; NONE when every day is a working day. When given with a calendar, it replaces the calendar's weekend.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar date counts.

reason.description: Why it is not a working day: holiday or weekend (holiday when both); empty on a working day.

actions.name: Next working day
actions.description: Return the first working day after a date in a business calendar, or the date itself when it is a working day and same_day is on. The time of day is kept.

calendar.description: Name of a holiday calendar in One CommandCenter (its holidays and weekend). Read once per run as the run's user; needs the agent to run from One CommandCenter. Leave empty to give the holidays and weekend here.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, as yyyy-MM-dd, e.g. ["2026-12-25"]. Added to the calendar's dates when a calendar is named too.

weekend.description: Days of the week that are not working days, e.g. SAT,SUN (the default) or FRI,SAT; NONE when every day is a working day. When given with a calendar, it replaces the calendar's weekend.

same_day.description: Return the date itself when it is a working day (e.g. a due date that moves only off holidays and weekends).

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar date counts; the time of day is kept in this zone.

actions.name: Get current date and time
actions.description: The date and time now. Show it in your time zone with Format date (Local, the runner's own, for new steps).

value.description: Current date and time in UTC.

actions.name: Text to date
actions.description: Read a date from text with a pattern such as dd/MM/yyyy, in the time zone the text is written in (Local, the runner's own, for new steps).

pattern.description: Pattern of the text, e.g. dd/MM/yyyy; needed unless a standard format is chosen.

time_zone.description: Time zone the text is in: local (the runner's own), UTC or a name such as Asia/Kolkata.

locale.description: Language of month and day names in the text, e.g. en, de-DE.

standard.description: A predefined ISO or RFC format to read instead of the pattern; an offset in the text wins over time_zone.

actions.name: Previous working day
actions.description: Return the last working day before a date in a business calendar, or the date itself when it is a working day and same_day is on. The time of day is kept.

calendar.description: Name of a holiday calendar in One CommandCenter (its holidays and weekend). Read once per run as the run's user; needs the agent to run from One CommandCenter. Leave empty to give the holidays and weekend here.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, as yyyy-MM-dd, e.g. ["2026-12-25"]. Added to the calendar's dates when a calendar is named too.

weekend.description: Days of the week that are not working days, e.g. SAT,SUN (the default) or FRI,SAT; NONE when every day is a working day. When given with a calendar, it replaces the calendar's weekend.

same_day.description: Return the date itself when it is a working day.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar date counts; the time of day is kept in this zone.

actions.name: Start of period
actions.description: Return midnight at the start of the day, week (Monday), month or year containing a date.

actions.name: Subtract from date
actions.description: Subtract an amount of time from a date.

amount.description: Amount to subtract. Fractions are exact for milliseconds to weeks; months, years and business days take whole numbers.

unit.description: Unit of the amount; business_days skips Saturdays, Sundays and the holidays.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, e.g. ["2026-12-25"].

actions.name: Count working days
actions.description: Count the working days between two dates in a business calendar: the days after the start up to and including the end (the start too, when chosen). The count is negative when the end is before the start.

calendar.description: Name of a holiday calendar in One CommandCenter (its holidays and weekend). Read once per run as the run's user; needs the agent to run from One CommandCenter. Leave empty to give the holidays and weekend here.

holidays.description: Dates that are not working days, as yyyy-MM-dd, e.g. ["2026-12-25"]. Added to the calendar's dates when a calendar is named too.

weekend.description: Days of the week that are not working days, e.g. SAT,SUN (the default) or FRI,SAT; NONE when every day is a working day. When given with a calendar, it replaces the calendar's weekend.

include_start.description: Count the start date too when it is a working day (Monday to Friday of one week is then 5, not 4).

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar date counts.

conditions.description: True when the first date is later than the second.

value.description: Date to check. A date, a Date variable, or text in the pattern below.

other.description: Date to compare with. A date, a Date variable, or text in the pattern below.

time_zone.description: Time zone whose calendar dates are compared when include_time is off.

pattern.description: Pattern of dates written as text, e.g. dd/MM/yyyy; ISO dates (2026-11-21) and Date variables need none.

value.description: Date to check. A date, a Date variable, or text in the pattern below.

conditions.name: Within business hours
conditions.description: True between the start and end hours in the time zone, on weekdays (or every day).

time_zone.description: Time zone.

weekdays_only.description: Only Monday to Friday count; turn off for teams that work every day.

conditions.description: True when both dates are the same moment, or the same day when the time is not included.
