name: Mouse and keyboard
description: Click, type, press keys, capture the screen, use the clipboard and show dialogs on the desktop.

actions.name: Block input
actions.description: Stop the person's mouse and keyboard from interfering while the next steps run. Windows allows it only to agents running as administrator; input comes back after the time limit, with Unblock input, or when the run ends, and Ctrl+Alt+Del always works.

seconds.description: Longest time to block, 1 to 300 seconds.

actions.name: Capture screen
actions.description: Save a screenshot of the whole screen, all screens, a region or a window as a PNG, JPEG or BMP file.

x.description: Region left (whole screen when empty).

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file; when false an existing file stops the step.

all_screens.description: Capture every monitor together instead of the main one (when no region or window is given).

window.description: Capture only this window (title text, pattern with * or ?, or re:regex); x and y are then measured from the window and default to its whole area.

jpeg_quality.description: JPEG quality from 1 (smallest file) to 100 (best picture).

actions.name: Clear clipboard
actions.description: Empty the clipboard.

actions.name: Get clipboard text
actions.description: Read text from the clipboard, optionally waiting until text arrives (e.g. after pressing CTRL+C).

wait_seconds.description: Keep checking up to this long while the clipboard is empty or busy; 0 reads once.

trim.description: Remove spaces and line breaks at both ends.

text.description: Clipboard text, empty when it holds no text.

has_text.description: True when the clipboard held text.

actions.name: Copy to clipboard
actions.description: Put text on the clipboard, replacing it or adding to what is there.

append.description: Add the text after the current clipboard text instead of replacing it.

actions.name: Get mouse position
actions.description: Return where the mouse pointer is, in the same screen pixels Mouse click and Mouse move use.

x.description: Pixels from the left of the main screen.

y.description: Pixels from the top of the main screen.

actions.name: Message box
actions.description: Show a message to the person at the screen with a choice of buttons and an icon; it can close by itself after some seconds.

message.description: Message text; it can be selected and copied.

title.description: Title shown in bold at the top and as the window's title; the agent's name when empty.

timeout_seconds.description: Close by itself after this many seconds, showing the time left; 0 waits for a button.

buttons.description: Buttons to show; Enter presses the first, Esc means cancel or no.

icon.description: Icon next to the title; it also colours the top edge.

scroll_after_lines.description: Show the message in a scroll box when it has more lines than this; 0 never scrolls.

always_on_top.description: Keep the dialog in front of other windows.

button.description: Button chosen: ok, cancel, yes or no; closed when the window was closed; timeout when it closed by itself.

actions.name: Mouse click
actions.description: Click, double-click, or press or release a mouse button at a point on the screen or in a window.

x.description: Horizontal position in pixels from the left.

y.description: Vertical position in pixels from the top.

button_action.description: click presses and releases; down only presses (hold, e.g. to start a drag); up only releases.

relative_to.description: screen: x and y are measured from the top-left of the screen; window: from the top-left of the chosen window.

window.description: Window to bring to the front first: text in its title, a pattern with * or ?, or re:regex. Empty uses the window that is in front.

modifier_keys.description: Keys held during the click, e.g. CTRL, SHIFT or CTRL+SHIFT.

window_width.description: Outer width the window is given first, in pixels (with window_height), so a point measured from its corner lands where it was taken; Pick on screen fills it in.

window_height.description: Outer height the window is given first, in pixels (with window_width).

more.tick: Put the window back to this size first

actions.name: Mouse move
actions.description: Move the pointer to a point on the screen or in a window, at once or gradually.

x.description: Horizontal position.

relative_to.description: screen: x and y are measured from the top-left of the screen; window: from the top-left of the chosen window.

window.description: Window to bring to the front first: text in its title, a pattern with * or ?, or re:regex. Empty uses the window that is in front.

duration_ms.description: Glide to the point over this many milliseconds; 0 jumps there at once.

from_x.description: Put the pointer at this point first (with from_y, measured like x and y), then move to x, y; e.g. after pressing a button down, for a drag.

from_y.description: Vertical position of the starting point (with from_x).

window_width.description: Outer width the window is given first, in pixels (with window_height), so a point measured from its corner lands where it was taken; Pick on screen fills it in.

window_height.description: Outer height the window is given first, in pixels (with window_width).

more.tick: Put the window back to this size first

actions.name: Mouse scroll
actions.description: Scroll the mouse wheel up, down, left or right, optionally over a chosen point or window.

amount.description: Wheel notches; negative scrolls up (or left) when direction is empty.

direction.description: Scroll direction; when empty the sign of amount decides (positive scrolls down). Left and right hold SHIFT while scrolling.

x.description: Move the pointer here before scrolling (with y).

y.description: Vertical position to scroll at (with x).

relative_to.description: screen: x and y are measured from the top-left of the screen; window: from the top-left of the chosen window.

window.description: Window to bring to the front first: text in its title, a pattern with * or ?, or re:regex. Empty uses the window that is in front.

delay_ms.description: Pause between notches; 0 scrolls all notches at once.

window_width.description: Outer width the window is given first, in pixels (with window_height), so a point measured from its corner lands where it was taken; Pick on screen fills it in.

window_height.description: Outer height the window is given first, in pixels (with window_width).

more.tick: Put the window back to this size first

actions.name: Press keys
actions.description: Press, hold down or release a key or key combination, e.g. ENTER, CTRL+S or ALT+F4, in the active or a chosen window; repeat if needed.

key_action.description: press presses and releases; down holds the keys; up releases keys held by an earlier step.

hold_ms.description: How long to keep the keys down on each press.

window.description: Window to bring to the front first: text in its title, a pattern with * or ?, or re:regex. Empty uses the window that is in front.

actions.name: Prompt for file
actions.description: Ask the user to choose one or more files, optionally of given types.

title.description: Title shown in bold at the top; the window's title is the agent's name unless you change this.

file_types.description: Only show files with these extensions; all files when empty.

multiple.description: Let the user choose several files; paths lists them all.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds; 0 waits.

always_on_top.description: Keep the dialog in front of other windows.

message.description: Text shown in the dialog above the list, e.g. what to choose and why.

path.description: Chosen file (the first one when several), empty when cancelled.

cancelled.description: True when cancelled or timed out.

actions.name: Prompt for folder
actions.description: Ask the user to choose a folder.

title.description: Title shown in bold at the top; the window's title is the agent's name unless you change this.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds; 0 waits.

always_on_top.description: Keep the dialog in front of other windows.

message.description: Text shown in the dialog above the list, e.g. what to choose and why.
examples: Pick the folder with the scanned invoices.

cancelled.description: True when cancelled or timed out.

actions.name: Prompt for password
actions.description: Ask the user for a password; the result is a Credential that is never shown or logged.

title.description: Title shown in bold at the top and as the window's title; the agent's name when empty.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds (the step then fails as cancelled); 0 waits.

always_on_top.description: Keep the dialog in front of other windows.

password.description: Entered password as a Credential.

actions.name: Prompt for value
actions.description: Ask the user to type a value, optionally hidden as it is typed.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds; 0 waits.

title.description: Title shown in bold at the top and as the window's title; the agent's name when empty.

masked.description: Show dots instead of the typed characters. The value is still plain text; use Prompt for password for secrets.

always_on_top.description: Keep the dialog in front of other windows.

cancelled.description: True when the user cancelled or the prompt timed out.

timed_out.description: True when nobody answered in time; value is then the default.

actions.name: Prompt for yes/no
actions.description: Ask the user a yes/no question.

timeout_seconds.description: Answer No after this many seconds; 0 waits.

title.description: Title shown in bold at the top and as the window's title; the agent's name when empty.

always_on_top.description: Keep the dialog in front of other windows.

answer_on_timeout.description: Answer used when the prompt times out or is closed without a choice.

timed_out.description: True when nobody answered before the timeout (or the window was closed).

actions.name: Set lock keys
actions.description: Turn Caps Lock, Num Lock or Scroll Lock on or off, so text typed later comes out as expected.

was_on.description: Whether the key was on before.

actions.name: Show callout
actions.description: Show a small note pointing at a place on the screen for a few seconds, e.g. to tell the person in an attended run which field the agent is about to fill. It takes no clicks and does not take the focus.

text.description: Text of the note; a few words work best.
examples: Filling in the invoice number here

x.description: Point the note at: pixels from the left; the mouse pointer when x and y are empty.

y.description: Point the note at: pixels from the top.

relative_to.description: screen: x and y are measured from the top-left of the screen; window: from the top-left of the chosen window.

window.description: Window to bring to the front first: text in its title, a pattern with * or ?, or re:regex. Empty uses the window that is in front.

wait.description: Wait until the note has gone before the next step; by default the agent carries on while it shows.

actions.name: Type text
actions.description: Type text, or a credential from the vault, into the active or a chosen window (text is pasted via the clipboard by default, which handles any language; a credential is always typed key by key and never logged); can include special keys such as [ENTER].

text.description: Text to type; used when no credential is given.

method.description: paste uses the clipboard (restored afterwards); keystrokes types letters and digits one by one.

window.description: Window to bring to the front first: text in its title, a pattern with * or ?, or re:regex. Empty uses the window that is in front.

special_keys.description: Read keys in square brackets: [ENTER], [TAB 3], [CTRL+S], [SHIFT DOWN] ... [SHIFT UP]; [[ types a [.

restore_clipboard.description: With paste, put the previous clipboard content back afterwards.

delay_before_ms.description: Wait this long after bringing the window to the front, before typing.

credential.description: Credential attribute from the vault, e.g. a password; typed key by key (never through the clipboard) instead of text.

actions.name: Unblock input
actions.description: Give the mouse and keyboard back after Block input, before its time limit.

was_blocked.description: True when input was blocked by this run.

actions.name: Wait for mouse or key
actions.description: Pause until the person at the runner presses a chosen key, any key, or clicks the mouse, e.g. 'press F9 when the form is ready' in an attended agent.

wait_for.description: key: the key below; any_key: any key; click: any mouse button; key_or_click: the key below or a click.

key.description: Key name, e.g. F9, ENTER, ESC or A.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds.

fail_on_timeout.description: Fail with DESKTOP.INPUT_TIMEOUT when nothing happens in time; when off, timed_out is true and the agent carries on.

timed_out.description: True when nothing happened in time.

input.description: What happened: the key name, LEFT_CLICK, RIGHT_CLICK or MIDDLE_CLICK; empty on time-out.

x.description: Pointer position (physical screen pixels) when it happened.

y.description: Pointer position (physical screen pixels) when it happened.

name: Desktop objects
description: Capture controls in Windows applications and find them again by their UI Automation properties to click, type, read and select.

actions.name: Find legacy (MSAA) objects
actions.description: List the controls of an older application through MSAA (IAccessible), for programs UI Automation does not describe well: name, role, value, default action, state and position, each with its path.

window_title.description: Title of the application window: text it contains, or a pattern with * and ?.

name.description: Name of the control (contains, or * and ?); empty for any.

role.description: MSAA role, e.g. push button, editable text, list item, check box (contains, or * and ?).

value.description: Value of the control (contains, or * and ?); empty for any.

process.description: Program of the window, e.g. myerp.exe (optional, narrows the search).

objects.description: Matching objects: path, name, role, value, description, default_action, state, unavailable, checked, invisible, focusable, bounds.

actions.name: Find desktop objects
actions.description: Return every control that matches the object's used properties (the index is ignored), with their recorded properties.

object.description: The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for at least one match, in seconds; 0 looks once.

objects.description: One dictionary of properties per matching control, in the order UI Automation lists them.

actions.name: Get object properties
actions.description: Find a captured control and return all its current UI Automation properties and states.

object.description: The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the object to appear, in seconds.

properties.description: Current properties: the recorded ones plus states such as IsReadOnly, ToggleState, IsSelected, ExpandCollapseState and SupportedPatterns.

actions.name: Get parent object
actions.description: Find a captured control and return the control that contains it, one or more levels up or the nearest of a given type (for example the panel or table row around a label), as an object the other Desktop objects actions accept.

object.description: The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

levels.description: How many levels to go up: 1 is the direct container.

control_type.description: Go up to the nearest container of this type instead, e.g. Pane, Group, DataItem, Table, List, Window.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the object to appear, in seconds.

parent.description: The containing control as a captured object: pass it to Desktop object action, Get desktop table and the others.

control_type.description: Its type, e.g. Pane, Group, DataItem.

automation_id.description: Its AutomationId; empty when it has none.

levels_up.description: How many levels above the control it is.

options.label: To the nearest of a type

actions.name: Get desktop table
actions.description: Read a grid, table or detailed list view in a Windows application into a Data Table.

object.description: The captured grid, table or list control. The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the object to appear, in seconds.

table.description: The cell texts; columns are named after the grid's column headers.

actions.name: Get text at a point
actions.description: Read the text of whatever control is at a point on the screen, e.g. a scrolling text area or a label (G4).

x.description: Screen position from the left, in pixels.

y.description: Screen position from the top, in pixels.

actions.name: Legacy (MSAA) object action
actions.description: Act on a control of an older application through MSAA: its default action (press a button, check a box), set or get its value, select it, or read its properties. Find it by name and role, or by path.

window_title.description: Title of the application window: text it contains, or a pattern with * and ?.

name.description: Name of the control (contains, or * and ?).

role.description: MSAA role, e.g. push button, editable text, list item, check box (contains, or * and ?).

index.description: Which match to use when several do, 0 for the first.

path.description: The object's path from Find legacy objects, instead of name and role.

action.description: default_action presses, checks or opens it as the application defines; set_value types the value into it.

process.description: Program of the window, e.g. myerp.exe (optional, narrows the search).

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the window and the control, in seconds.

result.description: The value read (get_value), the properties (get_properties), or true.

object.description: The object acted on: path, name, role, value and the rest.

actions.name: Desktop object action
actions.description: Find a captured control in a Windows application and act on it: click, set or read text, read properties, select, expand, toggle, check, list items, read a grid, wait for it or get its position.

object.description: The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

action.description: What to do with the object.

click_method.description: click: pattern presses the control through UI Automation without moving the mouse (left click only); mouse moves the pointer and clicks; auto uses a pattern when the control offers one, else the mouse.

offset_x.description: click with the mouse: pixels right of the object's centre (negative for left).

offset_y.description: click with the mouse: pixels below the object's centre (negative for above).

text.description: set_text: the text to enter (a Credential is accepted and never logged).

clear_first.description: set_text: remove the existing text first; false appends.

text_method.description: set_text: set_value writes the value directly through UI Automation; type sends key presses one character at a time; auto writes directly when the control allows it, else types.

type_delay_ms.description: set_text with typing: pause between characters in milliseconds.

property.description: get_property: the property to read, e.g. Name, Value, IsEnabled, ToggleState, IsSelected, ExpandCollapseState.

item.description: select_item: the text of the item to select in a list, combo box, tree or tab control.

item_index.description: select_item: the position of the item to select (0 is the first), used when item is empty.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the object to appear, in seconds. For wait_disappear, how long to wait for it to go.

if_not_found.description: When the object is not there in time: error stops with an error; continue skips this step (result is empty, found is false) and carries on.

run_in_background.description: Work through UI Automation only: the window is not brought to the front and the mouse and keyboard are not used, so the application can stay behind other windows or minimised. Clicks and text then need a control that supports it (a single left click; text set directly).

row.description: Grid cell actions: the row, 1 for the first (G4).

column.description: Grid cell actions: the column, 1 for the first (G4).

find_text.description: The text of the cell to find (an exact match first, else the first containing it) (G4).

scroll_amount.description: scroll: a line or a page at a time (G4).

index_from_one.description: item_index counts from 1 for the first item, as Get selected index does; off counts from 0 as older steps did (G4).

result.description: What the action returns: text for get_text, a value for get_property, a dictionary for get_all_properties and get_coordinates, a list for get_children and get_list_items, a table for get_table, true/false for the wait actions.

healed_by.description: Empty when the object was found by its used properties; otherwise the recorded property that found it (update the object).

found.description: False when the step was skipped because the object was not found (if_not_found = continue).

actions.name: Pick desktop object
actions.description: Design time: point at a control in any Windows application and press Ctrl+Shift+C. A red frame shows the control under the pointer. Returns the captured object, ready for the other Desktop objects actions.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the Ctrl+Shift+C press, in seconds.

screenshot.description: Include a PNG image of the control (base64) in the object.

highlight.description: Draw a red frame around the control under the pointer while picking.

object.description: The captured object: technology, window, properties (with match and use), path, index and screenshot.

actions.name: Record desktop actions
actions.description: Design time: records clicks and typing in a Windows application until Stop recording is pressed on the recording bar. With a window, that window comes to the front and only clicks and typing in its application (with its dialogs) are recorded; without one, everything on the desktop is. Each click or field becomes a Desktop object action step with the full captured object; password fields are never read.

timeout_seconds.description: The longest the recording may run, in seconds.

screenshot.description: Include a PNG image of each control (base64) in its object.

window_title.description: The window to record in, by its exact title (from the open-windows list).

process.description: The window's program (process name, such as notepad), to tell windows with the same title apart.

steps.description: The recorded steps (ooa.desktop_ui/object_action), ready to insert into an agent.

actions.name: Wait for desktop object
actions.description: Wait until a captured control appears, or until it disappears, in a Windows application.

object.description: The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

state.description: Wait for the object to appear or to disappear.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wait in seconds.

fail_on_timeout.description: Fail the step when the time runs out; false returns found = false instead.

found.description: True when the wait ended in the requested state; false after a timeout when fail_on_timeout is false.

conditions.name: Desktop object exists
conditions.description: True when the captured control can be found now in a Windows application (self-healing applies), and, when asked, is enabled or has the keyboard focus.

object.description: The captured object (from Pick object or OneAgentStudio's desktop capture): window, properties with match and use, path and index.

state.description: G1 (AA parity): what to check besides being there: nothing more, that it can be used (enabled), or that it has the keyboard focus.

wait_seconds.description: Keep trying this many seconds until it is so; 0 checks once (G4).

name: Dictionary
description: Put, get and remove key/value pairs.

actions.name: Get
actions.description: Read the value for a key, or a default when the key is missing.

default.description: Value to return when the key is missing.

ignore_case.description: Find the key without regard to upper/lower case.

fail_if_missing.description: Fail with DICT.KEY_NOT_FOUND instead of returning the default.

found.description: True when the key exists.

actions.name: Get keys
actions.description: List all keys of a dictionary, in the order they were added.

actions.name: Merge
actions.description: Combine two dictionaries; for keys in both, keep the second value unless overwrite is off.

overwrite.description: Let values from the second dictionary replace existing ones.

actions.name: Put
actions.description: Add or replace the value for a key.

key.description: Key to set; added when the dictionary does not have it yet, its value replaced when it does (keys are case-sensitive).

only_if_missing.description: Keep the existing value when the key is already there.

position.description: G1 (AA parity): where a new key goes, counted from 0 (0 = first); at the end when empty. A key already there keeps its place.

previous.description: The value the key had before, empty when the key is new.

existed.description: True when the key was already there.

actions.name: Remove
actions.description: Remove a key and its value from a dictionary; returns the dictionary without it.

fail_if_missing.description: Fail with DICT.KEY_NOT_FOUND when the key is not there.

position.description: G1 (AA parity): remove the key at this place, counted from 0, instead of naming it.

removed.description: The value that was removed, empty when the key was not there.

found.description: True when the key was there.

actions.name: Get size
actions.description: Number of keys.

actions.name: Get values
actions.description: List all values.

values.description: Values in insertion order.

conditions.name: Contains key
conditions.description: True when the dictionary has the key.

conditions.name: Contains value
conditions.description: True when any key of the dictionary holds this value.

conditions.name: Dictionary is empty
conditions.description: True when the dictionary has no keys.

conditions.name: Key has value
conditions.description: True when the key exists and holds this value.

name: DLL
description: Call a function in a trusted native library (DLL) with numbers and text, and get its return value.

actions.name: Call DLL function
actions.description: Call an exported function, e.g. user32.dll MessageBeep, with typed arguments; returns its value.

library.description: Library name or full path of the DLL (or use session).

arguments.description: Arguments in order: plain values (whole numbers are int, other numbers double, text a Unicode string, true/false bool) or {"type": "int|long|double|bool|string|wstring", "value": ...} to choose the type.

session.description: Session from Open DLL; used instead of library.

calling_convention.description: How the function expects its arguments; matters only for 32-bit DLLs (Win32 API functions use stdcall).

result.description: Return value (number or text; empty for void).

actions.name: Close DLL
actions.description: Unload a library opened with Open DLL.

actions.name: Open DLL
actions.description: Load a trusted native library once as a named session, so several Call DLL function steps can use it.

library.description: Library name or full path of the DLL.

path.description: Name or path the library was loaded from.

name: Document Automation
description: Send documents (PDF, PNG, JPG, TIFF) to a Document Automation process, then pick up what it read: fields, tables and confidence, once read or reviewed.

actions.name: Download document
actions.description: Save a document's results (CSV or JSON), or the file that was sent, to a folder (G6). A file of the same name there is replaced.

document_id.description: The document id that Send document to process gave (or a document_id input given by a Start-a-bot delivery).

kind.description: csv: one row per field (field, value, confidence, page, corrected). json: everything that was read. original: the document as it was sent.

folder.description: The folder to save in. Empty: the run's temporary folder (the path output says where).

delete_after.description: Ask Document Automation to remove its copy once the file is saved. When the service keeps documents, the step says so and goes on.

deleted.description: True when Document Automation's copy was removed.

actions.name: Get document result
actions.description: Read a document's status and what Document Automation read from it, by its id: fields, tables (such as line items) and each field's confidence.

document_id.description: The document id that Send document to process gave (or a document_id input given by a Start-a-bot delivery).

status.description: queued or processing (still being read), success (read and checked), validation (waits for a reviewer), validated (approved), invalid (rejected) or failed.

done.description: True when the document is no longer being read.

needs_review.description: True while it waits for a person's review.

reviewed.description: True when a person approved or rejected it.

fields.description: The fields read, by name (after review: the corrected values).

tables.description: Table fields (such as line items), by name, each a Data table.

confidence.description: How sure the reading was for each field, from 0 to 1.

document_type.description: The document type it was classified as.

reviewed_by.description: Who approved or rejected it, when reviewed.

error.description: Why reading failed, when it failed.

actions.name: List finished documents
actions.description: List a process's documents that are read and need nothing more (read and checked, approved or rejected) and are not yet marked collected.

process.description: The process's name (or id) as shown in Document Automation.

reviewed_only.description: Only documents a person approved or rejected (not those read and checked without a review).

collector.description: A name for whoever collects: agents with the same name share the collected marks, so none takes a document twice. Empty: default.

include_collected.description: Also list documents already marked collected.

documents.description: Columns: document_id, file_name, status, document_type, created_at, reviewed_by, collected.

document_ids.description: The documents' ids, for a loop or for Mark collected.

actions.name: Mark collected
actions.description: Mark documents as collected, so List finished documents leaves them out for the same collector name.

document_ids.description: The ids to mark (a list, or one id).

collector.description: A name for whoever collects: agents with the same name share the collected marks, so none takes a document twice. Empty: default.

marked.description: How many documents were marked now.

actions.name: Send document to process
actions.description: Send a document to a live Document Automation process. Optionally wait until it is read, to use its fields and status in the agent.

process.description: The process's name (or id) as shown in Document Automation. It must be live.

path.description: The document: PDF, PNG, JPG or TIFF.

wait.description: Wait until the document is read (up to 15 minutes) and return its status and fields.

process_version.description: Only send when the process's setup is still this version (G6), so a changed setup never reads the document unnoticed: a different version stops the step with DOCS.VERSION_CHANGED. Empty: whatever version is live.

document_id.description: The document's id in Document Automation.

status.description: processing, success (read and checked), validation (waits for a reviewer), invalid or failed.

needs_review.description: True when a person must review it (only known when waiting).

fields.description: The fields read, by name (only when waiting).

actions.name: Update document result
actions.description: Write corrected field values back to a read document (G6). The values are kept as a review by the run's user, so the document then counts as approved.

document_id.description: The document id that Send document to process gave (or a document_id input given by a Start-a-bot delivery).

fields.description: The corrected values by field name: a Dictionary, or JSON text such as {"total": "110.00"}. Fields left out keep their values.

status.description: The document's status after the change (validated when approved).

fields.description: The document's fields after the change, by name.

actions.name: Wait for document
actions.description: Wait until a document is read, or until it is also reviewed when it needs a review, then give its result.

document_id.description: The document id that Send document to process gave (or a document_id input given by a Start-a-bot delivery).

until.description: Read: until it is read (it may then wait for a review). Reviewed: also until a person has reviewed it, when it needs a review.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds with the error DOCS.WAIT_TIMEOUT (a review may take hours).

check_every_seconds.description: How often to ask Document Automation.

status.description: The document's status when the wait ended.

done.description: True when the document is no longer being read.

needs_review.description: True while it waits for a person's review.

reviewed.description: True when a person approved or rejected it.

fields.description: The fields read, by name.

tables.description: Table fields (such as line items), by name, each a Data table.

confidence.description: How sure the reading was for each field, from 0 to 1.

document_type.description: The document type it was classified as.

reviewed_by.description: Who approved or rejected it, when reviewed.

error.description: Why reading failed, when it failed.

name: DocuSign
description: Send documents for e-signature, track and manage envelopes and recipients, use templates and download signed documents.

actions.name: Add recipients
actions.description: Add signers or copy recipients to an envelope that is still a draft or in progress, optionally in a signing order.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

recipients.description: Recipients: each {"name", "email", "type": signer or copy, "routing_order": 1, 2 ...}, e.g. [{"name": "Ann Lee", "email": "ann@acme.test"}].

resend.description: Send the request to the new recipients when the envelope is already sent.

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Sign in once with a saved connection: the later DocuSign steps of this agent use it unless they choose another.

connection.description: Saved connection (under Connections) that the later steps of this toolkit use when they choose none of their own.

session.description: A name for this sign-in; the toolkit's own when empty.

share.description: Agents this one runs may use it too.

connection.description: The saved connection the later steps use.

actions.name: Create envelope
actions.description: Prepare an envelope from local files and signers, then send it now or keep it as a draft.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

documents.description: Local files to sign, e.g. ["contracts/nda.pdf"]. PDF, Word and most office formats work.

signers.description: People who sign, in a list like [{"name": "Ann Lee", "email": "ann@acme.com"}]. Add routing_order to sign one after another.

email_subject.description: Subject of the signing request email.

email_message.description: Message shown in the signing request email.

copy_to.description: People who receive a copy when signing is finished, same format as signers.

sign_here_text.description: Text in the document where the signature box goes. Leave empty to let signers place it themselves.

send_now.description: Send right away. When off, the envelope is saved as a draft to send later.

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

status.description: sent or created (draft).

actions.name: Envelope from template
actions.description: Start an envelope from a saved template by filling each template role with a person.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

roles.description: Who fills each role, e.g. [{"role": "Client", "name": "Ann Lee", "email": "ann@acme.com"}].

field_values.description: Pre-filled text fields by their label, e.g. {"ContractNumber": "C-1042"}.

email_subject.description: Subject of the email. Leave empty to use the template's subject.

send_now.description: Send right away. When off, the envelope is saved as a draft.

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

status.description: sent or created (draft).

actions.name: Get embedded signing link
actions.description: Get a short-lived link that opens the signing session for a recipient inside your own app or portal.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

name.description: Signer's name exactly as on the envelope.

email.description: Signer's email exactly as on the envelope.

client_user_id.description: The client_user_id given to this signer when the envelope was created.

return_url.description: Page the signer goes to when they finish or leave.

authentication_method.description: How your app checked who the signer is, e.g. none, email or password.

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

url.description: Signing link; it works once and expires within minutes.

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: Forget the connection Connect chose; later DocuSign steps then use their own.

session.description: The sign-in's name; every one of this toolkit when empty.

actions.name: Download combined PDF
actions.description: Save all documents of an envelope as one PDF, optionally with the signing certificate at the end.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

save_as.description: Where to save the PDF, e.g. signed/all.pdf, or a folder; the run's temporary folder when empty (G5).

include_certificate.description: Add the signing certificate as the last pages.

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

path.description: Full path of the saved PDF.

actions.name: Download document
actions.description: Save one document from an envelope, the signing certificate, or all documents as a zip archive.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

document_id.description: Document number from List envelope documents, or certificate for the signing certificate, or archive for a zip of everything.

save_as.description: Where to save it, e.g. signed/contract.pdf, or a folder; the run's temporary folder when empty (G5). Missing folders are created.

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

path.description: Full path of the saved file.

actions.name: Download signed ZIP
actions.description: Save all documents of an envelope as separate PDFs in one ZIP file, with the signing certificate.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

save_as.description: Where to save the ZIP, e.g. signed/contract.zip, or a folder; the run's temporary folder when empty (G5).

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

path.description: Full path of the saved ZIP.

actions.name: Get envelope custom fields
actions.description: Read the custom fields stored on an envelope, such as a contract or order number.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

fields.description: Field name to value.

actions.name: Get envelope status
actions.description: Check where an envelope is: draft, sent, delivered, completed, declined or voided.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

status.description: created, sent, delivered, completed, declined or voided.

envelope.description: envelope_id, status, subject, sent, delivered, completed, voided_reason, status_changed.

actions.name: Get filled-in form data
actions.description: Read the values recipients typed into the envelope's fields, for example after it is completed.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

values.description: Field label to entered value.

actions.name: Get template
actions.description: Read a template's name, roles and documents, so you know which roles to fill.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

roles.description: Names of the roles to fill, e.g. ["Client", "Manager"].

actions.name: List envelope documents
actions.description: Return the documents inside an envelope.

base_url.description: Your account's REST address, e.g. https://demo.docusign.net/restapi for testing or https://na4.docusign.net/restapi in production. Leave empty to look it up from the account (production first, then the demo environment).

account_id.description: DocuSign account id (a GUID or number shown under Apps and Keys).

access_token.description: DocuSign OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

name: .NET, Java and COM
description: Run inline C# or VB.NET code, and call methods of .NET assemblies, COM objects and Java classes.

actions.name: Call COM method
actions.description: Create a COM object by its ProgID and call a method or read or set a property (Windows), optionally through a path of properties.

path.description: Properties to go through first, in order, e.g. Workbooks then Item.

kind.description: Call a method, read a property, or set one (its value is the last argument).

arguments.description: Arguments in order.

quit.description: Call the object's Quit method at the end (Office applications).

timeout_seconds.description: Stop the call after this many seconds.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the code throws; when off, the error goes to 'error' and the run goes on.

result.description: What the method or property returned (objects as text).

error.description: The error, when fail on error is off.

actions.name: Call .NET method
actions.description: Call a static method or property of a .NET type, or create an object and call one of its methods (Windows).

assembly.description: DLL path or assembly name; empty for types of the .NET Framework itself (System.Math).

type.description: Full type name, with its namespace.

kind.description: Call a method, or read a property or field.

arguments.description: Arguments in order; JSON numbers become Int32, Int64, Decimal or Double.

create_instance.description: Create an object of the type first and call the member on it.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop the call after this many seconds.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the code throws; when off, the error goes to 'error' and the run goes on.

result.description: What the method or property returned.

output.description: Anything the method wrote to the console.

error.description: The exception, when fail on error is off.

actions.name: Call Java method
actions.description: Load JAR files and call a static method of a class, or create an object and call one of its methods, in a separate Java process.

jars.description: JAR files or class folders to load; empty for classes of Java itself.

class_name.description: Full class name, with its package.

method.description: Method name; the one whose parameters fit the arguments is used.

arguments.description: Arguments in order; converted to the method's parameter types.

create_instance.description: Create an object of the class first and call the method on it.

java.description: Java program to use; the runner's own Java, then java on the PATH, when empty.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop the call after this many seconds.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the code throws; when off, the error goes to 'error' and the run goes on.

result.description: What the method returned (text, numbers, true/false, lists and maps; other objects as text).

error.description: The exception, when fail on error is off.

actions.name: Call method in session
actions.description: Call a static method of a type, or a method of an object created in the session, with typed and named arguments (G4).

session.description: Name of the .NET session, from Open assembly.

type.description: Full type name for a static method.

object_name.description: An object made with Create object.

arguments.description: Arguments in order.

argument_types.description: The type of each argument, in order: auto, text, int, long, double, decimal, bool, byte, datetime, bytes (base64), text_list, number_list, list or dictionary.

named_arguments.description: Arguments by their parameter names, after the ones in order.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time; the session is closed when it runs out.

output.description: Anything it wrote to the console.

options.label: A static method of a type
A method of a session object

actions.name: Close assembly
actions.description: End a .NET session (G4); sessions also end with the run.

session.description: Name of the .NET session, from Open assembly.

actions.name: Create object
actions.description: Create an object of a type of the open assembly and keep it in the session by a name, for Call method (G4).

session.description: Name of the .NET session, from Open assembly.

type.description: Full type name, with its namespace.

object_name.description: Name the object is kept by.

arguments.description: Constructor arguments in order.

argument_types.description: The type of each argument, in order: auto, text, int, long, double, decimal, bool, byte, datetime, bytes (base64), text_list, number_list, list or dictionary.

named_arguments.description: Arguments by their parameter names, after the ones in order.

actions.name: Open assembly
actions.description: Load a .NET assembly (DLL) into a session kept for the steps after it, so objects it creates keep their state (G4, Windows).

session.description: Session name the later steps use.

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same session.

actions.name: Read assembly
actions.description: List the public types of a .NET assembly with their methods and parameters (G4).

types.description: Each type: type (full name) and methods (name, static, returns, parameters with name, type, optional).

actions.name: Run C# code
actions.description: Run C# statements (the body of a method that gets args and returns a value); compiled by the .NET Framework on Windows.

code.description: C# statements; args is an IDictionary<string, object> of the arguments; return a value.

arguments.description: Values the code reads as args["name"].

usings.description: Extra namespaces, one per line (System, Collections.Generic, Linq, Text and IO are there).

members.description: Other methods or fields of the same static class, for code used more than once.

references.description: Assemblies the code needs beyond the usual ones: names such as System.Xml, or DLL paths.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop the call after this many seconds.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the code throws; when off, the error goes to 'error' and the run goes on.

result.description: What the code returns (text, numbers, true/false, lists and dictionaries; other objects as text).

output.description: What the code wrote with Console.WriteLine.

error.description: The exception, when fail on error is off.

actions.name: Run VB.NET code
actions.description: Run VB.NET statements (the body of a function that gets args and returns a value); compiled by the .NET Framework on Windows.

code.description: VB.NET statements; args is an IDictionary(Of String, Object) of the arguments; Return a value.
examples:
Dim n As Integer = CInt(args("count"))
Return n * 2

references.description: Assemblies the code needs beyond the usual ones: names or DLL paths.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the code throws; when off, the error goes to 'error' and the run goes on.

result.description: What the code returns (text, numbers, true/false, lists and dictionaries; other objects as text).

output.description: What the code wrote with Console.WriteLine.

error.description: The exception, when fail on error is off.

importance.description: Importance shown by the recipient's mail program.
