name: Kafka
description: Send messages to Kafka topics, read messages, and create or inspect topics through a Kafka REST Proxy.

actions.name: Commit offsets
actions.description: Record, for a consumer group, that one partition of a topic has been handled up to and including an offset, so the next read starts after it. Use it with Read messages and mark_as_read off to mark messages only once they are processed, or to skip ahead or go back. Run it while no other reader of the group is active. Needs a REST Proxy that supports consumer instances.

base_url.description: Kafka REST Proxy address, e.g. https://pkc-12345.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443 or http://kafka-rest.internal:8082.

consumer_group.description: Reader group whose position is changed.

partition.description: Partition number, as shown in the partition column of Read messages.

offset.description: Offset of the last message handled in that partition; the group carries on with the message after it.

api_key.description: API key or user name, used with api_secret.

api_secret.description: API secret or password from the vault.

access_token.description: Bearer token from the vault, used instead of an API key and secret.

next_offset.description: Offset the group reads next in that partition (offset + 1).

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Keep the address and sign-in under a session for the steps after it, so they need not repeat them (G6).

base_url.description: The base url the later steps use (G6).

api_key.description: The api key the later steps use (G6).

api_secret.description: The api secret the later steps use (G6).

access_token.description: The access token the later steps use (G6).

cluster_id.description: The cluster id the later steps use (G6).

session.description: The session's name; the toolkit's default session when empty.

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same session.

actions.name: Create topic
actions.description: Create a topic with a number of partitions and optional settings such as how long messages are kept.

base_url.description: Kafka REST Proxy address, e.g. https://pkc-12345.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443 or http://kafka-rest.internal:8082.

partitions.description: Number of partitions; more partitions let more readers work in parallel.

replication_factor.description: Copies of each message kept on different servers. Leave empty for the cluster default.

fail_if_exists.description: Stop with an error if the topic is already there, instead of carrying on.

cluster_id.description: Kafka cluster id. Leave empty to use the only (first) cluster the proxy serves.

api_key.description: API key or user name, used with api_secret.

api_secret.description: API secret or password from the vault.

access_token.description: Bearer token from the vault, used instead of an API key and secret.

created.description: True if the topic was created, false if it was already there.

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: Forget the open Kafka session; later steps then need their own address and sign-in (G6).

session.description: The session; the toolkit's default session when empty.

closed.description: True when a session was open.

actions.name: Get topic info
actions.description: Read a topic's partition count, replication and settings.

base_url.description: Kafka REST Proxy address, e.g. https://pkc-12345.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443 or http://kafka-rest.internal:8082.

cluster_id.description: Kafka cluster id. Leave empty to use the only (first) cluster the proxy serves.

api_key.description: API key or user name, used with api_secret.

api_secret.description: API secret or password from the vault.

access_token.description: Bearer token from the vault, used instead of an API key and secret.

settings.description: Topic settings, e.g. retention.ms and cleanup.policy.

actions.name: List topics
actions.description: Return the topics in the cluster.

base_url.description: Kafka REST Proxy address, e.g. https://pkc-12345.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443 or http://kafka-rest.internal:8082.

include_internal.description: Also list Kafka's own internal topics, whose names usually start with an underscore.

cluster_id.description: Kafka cluster id. Leave empty to use the only (first) cluster the proxy serves.

api_key.description: API key or user name, used with api_secret.

api_secret.description: API secret or password from the vault.

access_token.description: Bearer token from the vault, used instead of an API key and secret.

actions.name: Send message
actions.description: Write one message to a topic, with an optional key and headers.

base_url.description: Kafka REST Proxy address, e.g. https://pkc-12345.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443 or http://kafka-rest.internal:8082.

value.description: Message content: text, or a dictionary or list sent as JSON.

key.description: Message key. Messages with the same key always go to the same partition, so they stay in order.

value_format.description: Send the value as JSON or as plain text.

partition.description: Write to this partition. Leave empty to let Kafka choose.

cluster_id.description: Kafka cluster id. Leave empty to use the only (first) cluster the proxy serves.

api_key.description: API key or user name, used with api_secret.

api_secret.description: API secret or password from the vault.

access_token.description: Bearer token from the vault, used instead of an API key and secret.

partition.description: Partition the message was written to.

offset.description: Position of the message in that partition.

timestamp.description: Time Kafka recorded for the message.

actions.name: Read messages
actions.description: Read new messages from one or more topics as a consumer group, so the next read carries on where this one stopped. Needs a REST Proxy that supports consumer instances (self-managed Confluent REST Proxy).

base_url.description: Kafka REST Proxy address, e.g. https://pkc-12345.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443 or http://kafka-rest.internal:8082.

consumer_group.description: Reader group name. Agents with the same group share the work and never get the same message twice.

max_messages.description: Stop once this many messages have arrived. The last batch is kept whole, so a few more can come back.

wait_seconds.description: Stop when no new message arrives within this time.

value_format.description: Read values as JSON or as plain text.

start_from.description: For a new group only: start at the oldest message kept (earliest) or only new messages (latest).

mark_as_read.description: Remember what was read so the group does not read it again.

api_key.description: API key or user name, used with api_secret.

api_secret.description: API secret or password from the vault.

access_token.description: Bearer token from the vault, used instead of an API key and secret.

csv_file.description: Also save the messages read to this CSV file (topic, partition, offset, key, value), replacing it; no file when empty (G6).

table.description: Columns: topic, partition, offset, key, value. JSON values are shown as text.

messages.description: Each message as a dictionary; JSON values stay structured.

csv_file.description: The CSV file written; empty when csv_file was not given (G6).

name: Knowledge Q&A
description: Index your documents and answer questions from them, with the passages each answer comes from.

actions.name: Ask
actions.description: Answer a question from a knowledge index: the best passages go to the model, which answers from them only and cites them.

index_file.description: The index file, e.g. knowledge/policies.json (.json.gz keeps it smaller).

top_k.description: How many passages the model gets.

connection.description: Name of a Model Connection (provider, model and key managed in one place). Leave empty to set them on this action.

provider.description: Who runs the model: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), Hugging Face (its router or your own TGI server), AWS SageMaker (a model on an Amazon SageMaker endpoint), AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI (Gemini).

model.description: Model name; the deployment name for Azure OpenAI; the endpoint name for AWS SageMaker; the model or inference profile id for AWS Bedrock.

api_key.description: API key or access token from the vault (not needed for some self-hosted endpoints). For AWS Bedrock and AWS SageMaker: the AWS secret access key (or ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET). For Google Vertex AI: a service-account JSON key or an access token.

base_url.description: Endpoint; required for Azure OpenAI, Vertex AI (https://REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT/locations/REGION) and self-hosted models (for a TGI server, e.g. http://tgi-host:8080/v1).

embedding_connection.description: The embedding connection, when not the one the index was built with.

mask_pii.description: Replace emails, phone and card numbers, IBANs and similar before sending; restored in the answer.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the model; 180 when 0.

knowledge_base.description: A knowledge base kept in One CommandCenter (AI > Knowledge bases), by name; in Studio without One CommandCenter, knowledge-bases/<name>.json.gz in the work folder.

sources.description: The passages given to the model: n, source, passage, score, text.

found.description: False when no passage matched, so the model was not asked.

actions.name: Build index
actions.description: Read documents (files or folders) and texts, split them into passages and write a knowledge index, with embeddings when a model connection is given.

files.description: Files and folders to read (folders with their sub-folders).

texts.description: Texts to add, each a dictionary with source and text (for example from the PDF or OCR toolkit).

index_file.description: The index file, e.g. knowledge/policies.json (.json.gz keeps it smaller).

connection.description: A saved model connection for embeddings, e.g. one for text-embedding-3-small; without one the index is searched by words only.

provider.description: Embedding provider, when not using a saved connection.

model.description: Embedding model (the deployment for Azure OpenAI).

api_key.description: API key or access token from the vault (not needed for some self-hosted endpoints). For AWS Bedrock and AWS SageMaker: the AWS secret access key (or ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET). For Google Vertex AI: a service-account JSON key or an access token.

base_url.description: Endpoint; required for Azure OpenAI, Vertex AI (https://REGION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT/locations/REGION) and self-hosted models (for a TGI server, e.g. http://tgi-host:8080/v1).

overlap.description: Characters each passage shares with the one before, so no sentence is cut off from its context.

mask_pii.description: Mask emails, phone and card numbers before they are sent for embedding (search by those then works by words only).

knowledge_base.description: A knowledge base kept in One CommandCenter (AI > Knowledge bases), by name; in Studio without One CommandCenter, knowledge-bases/<name>.json.gz in the work folder.

urls.description: Web pages to read (https:// addresses of intranet or public pages; HTML, text or PDF).

passages.description: How many passages the index holds.

skipped.description: Files that could not be read, with the reason.

options.label: A knowledge base in One CommandCenter

actions.name: Search
actions.description: Find the passages of a knowledge index that best answer a question, by words and, when the index has embeddings, by meaning.

index_file.description: The index file, e.g. knowledge/policies.json (.json.gz keeps it smaller).

query.description: The question or words to look for.

connection.description: The embedding connection, when not the one the index was built with.

api_key.description: The embedding API key, for an index built without a saved connection.

knowledge_base.description: A knowledge base kept in One CommandCenter (AI > Knowledge bases), by name; in Studio without One CommandCenter, knowledge-bases/<name>.json.gz in the work folder.

results.description: Best passages first: n, source, passage, score (0 to 1), text.

name: List
description: Add, read, remove, sort and join list items.

actions.name: Add item
actions.description: Add an item at the end, or at a position.

position.description: Zero-based position; end of list when empty.

items.description: Several items to add in one go, after 'item' when both are given.

skip_existing.description: Do not add an item that is already in the list.

actions.name: Append list
actions.description: Join two lists into one, the second after the first.

other.description: List to add at the end.

actions.name: Clear
actions.description: Return an empty list; map it back to the variable to empty it.

actions.name: Filter
actions.description: Keep the items that pass a test, such as greater than 100 or contains Acme; for a list of records, test one field.

operator.description: Test; matches takes a regular expression.

value.description: Value to compare with (not needed for empty/not_empty).

field.description: For a list of records (dictionaries): the field to test; the item itself when empty.

match_case.description: Compare text with upper/lower case taken into account.

actions.name: Get item
actions.description: Read the item at a position.

position.description: Zero-based position; negative counts from the end (-1 = last).

if_out_of_range.description: When the position is outside the list: fail with LIST.INDEX, or return the default.

default.description: Value returned for a position outside the list when if_out_of_range is default.

actions.name: Find item
actions.description: Return the zero-based position of the first (or last) item equal to a value.

ignore_case.description: Compare text without regard to upper/lower case.

last.description: Return the last matching position instead of the first.

index.description: Zero-based position, or -1 when the value is not in the list.

found.description: True when the value is in the list.

actions.name: Items in both lists
actions.description: Return the items of the first list that are also in the second, in the first list's order, each once.

actions.name: Join
actions.description: Join items into one text with a separator.

separator.description: Separator; \n and \t stand for a line break and a tab.

escape_sequences.description: Turn \n, \r and \t in the separator into a line break, carriage return and tab.

actions.name: Remove duplicates
actions.description: Keep the first occurrence of each value.

actions.name: Remove item
actions.description: Remove the item at a position, or every item equal to a value.

position.description: Position to remove.

value.description: Remove every item equal to this value.

all_occurrences.description: With a value: remove every equal item; when off, only the first.

removed.description: The removed item (by position), or a list of the removed items (by value).

actions.name: Reverse
actions.description: Return the items in reverse order.

actions.name: Select field
actions.description: Turn a list of records (dictionaries) into a list of one field's values, e.g. the e-mail of every customer.

field.description: Field name; a.b reads a field inside a field.

skip_missing.description: Leave out records without the field; when off they give an empty value, so the positions still match.

list.description: The field's values, in the same order.

actions.name: Set item
actions.description: Replace the item at a position.

position.description: Zero-based position.

previous.description: The item that was at that position before (G1, AA parity).

actions.name: Shuffle
actions.description: Return the items in a random order, e.g. to pick a random sample.

list.description: The same items in random order.

actions.name: Get size
actions.description: Number of items.

actions.name: Sort
actions.description: Sort items (numbers numerically, text alphabetically).

actions.name: Items not in other list
actions.description: Return the items of the first list that are not in the second, e.g. invoices not yet processed.

list.description: Items only in the first list.

conditions.name: List contains item
conditions.description: True when the list contains the value.

conditions.name: List is empty
conditions.description: True when the list has no items.

name: Environment locks
description: Named locks that one agent run holds at a time, so two runners never use the same single-user system together.

actions.name: Acquire lock
actions.description: Take a named lock so no other agent run uses the same system at the same time. Optionally wait until the run holding it gives it back. The lock is given back by Release lock, or when this agent ends. With One CommandCenter the lock is shared by every runner; in OneAgentStudio on its own it works on this computer only.

name.description: The lock's name, e.g. SAP production login. Names are compared without case.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the lock when another run holds it; 0 tries once.

lease_seconds.description: How long the lock is held at most. After it, another run may take the lock. Acquire it again to renew the lease.

comment.description: Why the lock is held, shown in One CommandCenter.

fail_if_not_acquired.description: Fail with LOCK.TIMEOUT when the lock is not acquired, instead of returning acquired false.

acquired.description: True when this run now holds the lock.

held_by.description: When not acquired: the run, runner and person holding it, and since when.

main.tick: Fail when the lock is not acquired

actions.name: Check lock
actions.description: See whether a lock is held, by which run, runner and person, and since when. A lock past its lease counts as free.

held.description: True when a run holds the lock.

mine.description: True when this run holds it.

held_by.description: The run, runner and person holding it, and since when; empty when free.

since.description: When it was taken (ISO 8601), or empty.

expires.description: When its lease runs out (ISO 8601), or empty.

actions.name: Release lock
actions.description: Give back a lock this run holds, so another run can take it. A lock this run does not hold is left alone: released is false and the log says why.

released.description: True when this run held the lock and gave it back.

conditions.name: Lock is held
conditions.description: True when a run (this one or another) holds the lock now.

name: Log to file
description: Write timestamped lines to a log file or to the run log in One CommandCenter; secrets are masked automatically.

actions.description: Attach name and value pairs, such as the invoice number or customer, to every following line of this run's log until they are removed, so the log can be searched and filtered by them. Adding a name again changes its value.

fields.description: Names and values; values are stored as text, credentials as ****.
Every log field now set.

actions.name: Log to One CommandCenter
actions.description: Add a message, with optional details, to this run's log so it appears in One CommandCenter with the run's activity.

message.description: Text to log; ${...} interpolation allowed.

level.description: Level of the log entry; CRITICAL and EMERGENCY are recorded as errors with the level named.

details.description: Extra name and value pairs added to the entry as JSON.

source.description: Short tag for where the entry comes from, shown in brackets before the message, e.g. [invoice-check].

variables_of_type.description: G2 (AA parity): also log the agent's variables of this type (all = every variable) after the message; credentials never.

actions.name: Log variables to file
actions.description: Write one name=value line per variable to a log file, to record the state of a run; credentials are written as ****.

title.description: Heading line written before the variables.

timestamp.description: Start the heading with the date and time.

overwrite.description: Replace the file instead of appending.

timestamp_format.description: Pattern for the date and time; ISO 8601 with time zone when empty.

all_of_type.description: Also write every variable of the bot declared with this type (all = every variable), in declaration order, after the ones listed in variables. Credentials are written as ****.

main.tick: Also log every variable of a type

actions.name: Remove log fields
actions.description: Stop attaching log fields to the following lines: the ones named, or all of them.

names.description: Field names to remove; all when empty.

fields.description: The log fields still set.

actions.name: Log to file
actions.description: Append (or overwrite with) a line in a text log file, with optional timestamp and level.

message.description: Text to log; ${...} interpolation allowed.

timestamp.description: Start the line with the date and time.

overwrite.description: Replace the file instead of appending.

encoding.description: File encoding: utf-8, utf-16le (Unicode, written with a byte-order mark) or ansi (the runner's code page). Match the existing file when appending.

timestamp_format.description: Pattern for the date and time; ISO 8601 with time zone when empty.

name: Long-running agents
description: Suspend an agent until a time, a task, a work item, another run or a callback URL is called, and carry on from the same step; only from One CommandCenter.

actions.name: Create callback URL
actions.description: Make a one-time web address that another system calls (HTTP POST with a JSON body) when its work is done. Give the address to that system, then use Wait for callback. The address is shown here only once and works once; One CommandCenter keeps only a fingerprint of it. Needs the Public address in Settings.

url.description: The address to POST to: https://ONE-COMMANDCENTER/api/callbacks/TOKEN. Treat it as a secret: whoever has it can resume the run.

callback_id.description: Give it to Wait for callback.

actions.name: Create task
actions.description: Put an approval or a form in the Task inbox for people to do, then use Wait for task to suspend until it is done. Assign it to user:NAME or role:NAME (several separated by commas).

kind.description: approval: approve or reject, with a comment; form: fill in the form's fields.

title.description: What the task is, as the inbox lists it.

assignee.description: Who may do it: user:NAME or role:NAME, several separated by commas.

form.description: For a form: {"fields": [{"id": "amount", "label": "Amount", "type": "number", "required": true}]}, as in workflow forms.

due_hours.description: Overdue after this many hours; never when empty.

task_id.description: Give it to Wait for task.

actions.name: Resume after delay
actions.description: Suspend the agent for a while, or until a date and time, without holding the runner; then carry on from this step. For short pauses use Delay instead.

delay_seconds.description: How long to wait, in seconds.

until.description: Or: when to carry on, a date and time (in the runner's time zone unless it has an offset).

pool.description: Carry on on any runner of this pool; on the same runner when empty.

resumed_by.description: resumed_by: what ended the wait (time, task, queue_item, job, callback, admin or timeout).

actions.name: Suspend until
actions.description: Suspend the agent until something happens, then carry on from this step in a new run with the same values. The run shows as Suspended and its runner is free while it waits. Not inside a loop, a Parallel block, a Catch or a Finally; close browsers, workbooks and files first.

kind.description: What to wait for: time, a Task inbox task, a work item, another run (job), or a callback URL being called.

ref.description: time: seconds from now or a date and time with its offset (2026-11-07T09:00:00+05:30); task: the task id; queue_item: the work item id; job: the run id; callback: the callback id.

timeout_seconds.description: Stop waiting after this many seconds; wait as long as it takes when empty.

on_timeout.description: error: the step fails with LONGRUN.TIMEOUT (catch it in a Try); continue: carry on with Timed out true.

pool.description: Carry on on any runner of this pool (name or id); on the same runner when empty.

resumed_by.description: resumed_by: what ended the wait (time, task, queue_item, job, callback, admin or timeout).

timed_out.description: True when the timeout ended the wait (with On timeout set to continue).

result.description: What ended the wait: the callback's JSON body; a task's status, outcome, result and completed_by; a work item's status, result and error; a run's status, outputs and error. Empty for a time or a timeout.

actions.name: Wait for callback

timed_out.description: True when the timeout ended the wait.

value.description: Value the device reports after the change.

actions.name: SNMP walk
actions.description: Read every object under an OID, e.g. a whole interface table, with repeated GETNEXT requests or, for v2c and v3, fewer GETBULK requests.

host.description: Device host name or IP address.

oid.description: Root OID of the subtree to read.

community.description: SNMP v1 or v2c community (text or a Credential); public when empty.

port.description: UDP port of the SNMP agent.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for each answer, in milliseconds.

security_user.description: SNMP v3 security user name (v3 uses it instead of a community).

auth_protocol.description: SNMP v3 sign-in protocol: none, md5, sha (SHA-1), sha256 or sha512.

auth_password.description: SNMP v3 sign-in password from the vault.

privacy_protocol.description: SNMP v3 privacy (encryption): none, des or aes128.

privacy_password.description: SNMP v3 privacy (encryption) password from the vault.

context_name.description: SNMP v3 context, when the device uses them; usually empty.

walk_type.description: getnext asks for one object per request and works with every version; getbulk (v2c and v3 only) asks for up to max_repetitions objects per request, which is much faster on large tables.

max_repetitions.description: With getbulk, how many objects to ask for in each request; lower it when the device answers tooBig or not at all.

scope.description: within: only objects under the starting OID; all: go on to the end of the device's tree (up to max_rows) (G4).

output_as.description: Text values as the device sent them (auto: text when readable, else hex), always as text, or always as hex bytes (G4).

log_file.description: Also write what was asked and answered to this text file (G4).

conditions.name: Host is reachable
conditions.description: True when the host answers a ping within the timeout.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds.

wait_seconds.description: Keep trying this many seconds until it answers; 0 tries once (G4).

conditions.name: Port is open
conditions.description: True when a TCP port accepts connections.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds.

name: Number
description: Calculate, round, format and generate numbers with exact decimal arithmetic.

actions.name: Calculate
actions.description: Work out a number: pick an operation (add, divide, power, round up, average, percent of ...) or write a formula such as ($price$ * $qty$) * (1 + $tax$ / 100).

operation.description: What to work out. Percent of: A percent of B. Percentage change: from A to B, in percent. Round, round up and round down use Decimals.

a.description: The first number (the only one for square root, absolute, negate, round and the parts).

b.description: The second number: what is added, subtracted, multiplied by, divided by, the power, or the whole for Percent of.

values.description: The numbers, as a List variable or [1, 2, 3]; empty items are left out.

formula.description: A calculation with variables, brackets and functions, e.g. ($price$ * $qty$) * (1 + $tax$ / 100) or round(average($prices$), 2).

decimals.description: Round the result half up to this many decimals; empty keeps it as it is (Round, Round up and Round down: 0 when empty).

actions.name: Decrement
actions.description: Subtract a step (1 by default) from a number.

actions.name: Format number
actions.description: Format a number as text with thousands separators and fixed decimals, e.g. 1,234.50.

locale.description: Locale for separators, e.g. en-US, de-DE, en-IN.

actions.name: Format as currency or unit
actions.description: Write a number as money (1,234.50 EUR in the locale's way), as a percentage (15%) or with a unit (12.5 kg).

style.description: Money, percentage or a number with a unit.

currency.description: Three-letter currency code, e.g. USD, EUR, GBP, INR, JPY.

unit.description: The unit, e.g. kg, hours, pcs, km/h.

locale.description: Locale for separators and symbol position, e.g. en-US, de-DE, en-IN, fr-FR.

decimals.description: Decimal places; empty: the currency's own (2 for EUR, 0 for JPY), 0 for percent, as given for units.

fraction.description: When ticked 0.15 shows as 15%; when not, 15 shows as 15%.

unit_before.description: Write the unit first, e.g. Rs 120 instead of 120 Rs.

actions.name: Increment
actions.description: Add a step (1 by default) to a number.

actions.name: Random number
actions.description: Generate a random number between min and max (inclusive), whole or with decimals.

decimals.description: Decimal places of the result; 0 gives a whole number.

actions.name: Round
actions.description: Round a number to a number of decimal places.

mode.description: Rounding mode; half_even is banker's rounding.

actions.name: Round to a step
actions.description: Round a number to the nearest step, e.g. prices to 0.05 or 0.99 endings, times to 15 minutes, quantities to a pack size.

step.description: The step, e.g. 0.05, 0.5, 10 or 12 (a pack of twelve).

direction.description: To the nearest step (halves go up), always up, or always down.

actions.name: List statistics
actions.description: Count, sum, average, minimum, maximum and median of a list of numbers, in one step.

values.description: The numbers, as a List variable (a table column from Column to list) or [1, 2, 3].

skip_non_numbers.description: Leave out items that are not numbers instead of failing.
skip_non_numbers.x-ooa-label: Skip text that is not a number

median.description: The middle one (the average of the two middle ones for an even count).

actions.name: Number to text
actions.description: Write a number as plain text, with fixed decimals or a pattern such as 0000 or #,##0.00.

pattern.description: Pattern with 0 for required digits and # for optional ones, e.g. 00000 or #,##0.00.

rounding.description: How extra decimals are dropped: rounded half up, or cut off (truncated).

actions.name: Number to words
actions.description: Write a number in English words, for cheques and invoices: 1,234.50 as one thousand two hundred thirty-four dollars and fifty cents (lakh and crore for India).

style.description: Amount: whole units and two-digit cents (dollars and cents); plain: the number as it is, decimals read digit by digit (point two five).

major_unit.description: Name of the whole units, e.g. dollars, euros, rupees; empty for none.

minor_unit.description: Name of the hundredths, e.g. cents, paise; empty leaves them out.

system.description: International (thousand, million, billion) or Indian (thousand, lakh, crore).

letter_case.description: One thousand ..., one thousand ..., ONE THOUSAND ... or One Thousand ....

conditions.name: Compare numbers
conditions.description: True when the comparison holds, e.g. Amount greater than or equal to 1000; with a tolerance, close numbers count as equal.

tolerance.description: Numbers this close count as equal, e.g. 0.01 for amounts in cents.

conditions.name: Number is between
conditions.description: True when the number lies between two others (the ends count unless you untick Include the ends).

inclusive.description: Count the ends themselves as between.

name: OCR
description: Read text from images, image URLs or the screen, and find or click text on the screen (Tesseract, or the OCR built into Windows when Tesseract is not installed).

actions.name: Act next to a label
actions.description: Find a label on the screen with OCR (e.g. Invoice number:) and click, type into or read the field next to it: for remote desktops and screens without accessible controls (G4).

label.description: The label's text as the screen shows it.

where.description: Where the field is from its label.

action.description: What to do with the field.

text.description: type: the text to type; it may come from the vault.

occurrence.description: Which appearance of the label, counting in reading order from 1.

gap.description: Pixels between the label and the field.

field_width.description: Width of the field in pixels.

field_height.description: Height of the field in pixels; a little more than the label when 0.

language.description: Tesseract language(s), e.g. eng, deu or eng+fra.

wait_seconds.description: Keep looking for the label this many seconds; 0 looks once.

y.description: Centre y of the field on the screen.

tesseract_languages.description: Tesseract languages, e.g. eng, deu; empty when Tesseract is not installed.

tesseract_path.description: The Tesseract program used, when installed.

count.description: How many times the phrase appears in the image.

email.description: New primary email address; unchanged when empty (G6).

first_name.description: New given name; unchanged when empty (G6).

last_name.description: New family name; unchanged when empty (G6).

phone.description: New mobile phone number (mobilePhone); unchanged when empty (G6).

user.description: The user after the change.

name: Outlook desktop
description: Find, read, send, reply to, forward, move and file emails with the Outlook installed on the runner, using its mail profile.

actions.name: Use mailbox

mailbox.description: A mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address); empty for the user's own.

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same mailbox.

actions.name: Delete email
actions.description: Delete an email (Outlook moves it to Deleted Items).

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

actions.name: Delete all emails
actions.description: Delete every email in a folder that the filters find (Outlook moves them to Deleted Items).

folder.description: Folder path.

subject_contains.description: Only emails whose subject contains this text.

from_contains.description: Only emails whose sender address or name contains this text.

received_after.description: Only emails received after this date and time.

received_before.description: Only emails received before this date and time (G3).

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

actions.name: Stop using mailbox
actions.description: Later Outlook desktop steps go back to the user's own mailbox, or the one each names.

actions.name: Forward email
actions.description: Forward an email with its attachments, with a note above it and more files if wanted; send it or keep it in Drafts.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

body.description: A note above the forwarded email.

save_as_draft.description: Keep it in Drafts instead of sending.

html.description: The note is HTML (bold, links, lists) (G3).

draft_id.description: The draft's id when it was kept as a draft, else empty.

actions.name: Read email
actions.description: Read one email: sender, recipients, subject, text and HTML body and attachment names.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

email.description: id, subject, from, from_name, to, cc, received, unread, body, html_body, categories, attachment_names, folder. Also, the same on every mail service: id, from, to, cc, subject, received, text, html, attachments (names), has_attachments, unread, message_id.

actions.name: Get folders
actions.description: List the folders of the mailbox with how many emails and unread emails each has.

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

folders.description: Folders: path (as Move email and Find emails take it), emails, unread.

actions.name: Find emails
actions.description: List the newest emails in an Outlook folder, optionally only unread ones, by subject, by sender or received after a date.

folder.description: Folder path: Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, or a folder below them, e.g. Inbox/Invoices.

subject_contains.description: Only emails whose subject contains this text.

from_contains.description: Only emails whose sender address or name contains this text.

received_after.description: Only emails received after this date and time.

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time.

received_before.description: Only emails received before this date and time (G3).

emails.description: Emails, newest first: id, subject, from, from_name, to, received, unread, attachments, folder.

table.description: The same emails as a table, as the other mail services give it: id, from, subject, received, unread, has_attachments.

actions.name: Mark read or unread
actions.description: Mark an email as read or unread, and optionally add an Outlook category to it.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

read.description: true marks it read, false unread.

category.description: An Outlook category to add, e.g. Processed.

actions.name: Move email
actions.description: Move an email to another folder, e.g. Inbox/Done. The email gets a new id.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

folder.description: Folder path to move it to.

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

id.description: The email's new id.

actions.name: Move all emails
actions.description: Move every email in a folder that the filters find to another folder, e.g. Inbox/Done. The emails get new ids.

folder.description: Folder path to move from.

to_folder.description: Folder path to move them to.

subject_contains.description: Only emails whose subject contains this text.

from_contains.description: Only emails whose sender address or name contains this text.

received_after.description: Only emails received after this date and time.

received_before.description: Only emails received before this date and time (G3).

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

to_mailbox.description: The mailbox of the folder to move to; the same mailbox when empty.

actions.name: Reply to email
actions.description: Reply to the sender (or everyone) above the original message, with copies and files if wanted; send it or keep it in Drafts.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

reply_all.description: Reply to everyone on the email.

save_as_draft.description: Keep it in Drafts instead of sending.

cc.description: Also copy to (G3), separated by semicolons.

html.description: The reply is HTML (bold, links, lists) (G3).

draft_id.description: The draft's id when it was kept as a draft, else empty.

actions.name: Save all emails
actions.description: Save every email in a folder that the filters find as files (.msg keeps the attachments), named after their subjects.

folder.description: Folder path.

save_to.description: Folder on the runner to save into.

format.description: File type: msg (Outlook, keeps attachments), txt, html or mht.

overwrite.description: Replace a file of the same name; off: the new file gets a number such as (1).

subject_contains.description: Only emails whose subject contains this text.

from_contains.description: Only emails whose sender address or name contains this text.

received_after.description: Only emails received after this date and time.

received_before.description: Only emails received before this date and time (G3).

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

actions.name: Save attachments
actions.description: Save an email's attachments to a folder, optionally only those matching a name pattern; existing files are kept and new ones numbered, or replaced.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

folder.description: Folder to save into.

name_pattern.description: Only attachments whose name matches, e.g. *.pdf.

overwrite.description: Replace a file of the same name; off: the new file gets a number such as (1). (G3)

actions.name: Save email
actions.description: Save one email as a file: .msg (opens in Outlook, keeps the attachments), text, HTML or MHT.

id.description: The email's id from Find emails.

save_to.description: Folder on the runner to save into.

format.description: File type: msg (Outlook, keeps attachments), txt, html or mht.

file_name.description: File name with its extension; the email's subject when empty.

overwrite.description: Replace a file of the same name; off: the new file gets a number such as (1).

actions.name: Send email
actions.description: Send an email from Outlook, or keep it in Drafts for someone to check, with attachments and optionally from another account of the profile.

from_account.description: Send from this account of the Outlook profile (its address); empty for the default.

save_as_draft.description: Keep it in Drafts instead of sending.

draft_id.description: The draft's id when it was kept as a draft, else empty.

conditions.name: Outlook folder exists
conditions.description: True when the mailbox has the folder, e.g. Inbox/Invoices.

folder.description: Folder path.

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

iterators.name: Each email in an Outlook folder
iterators.description: Go through the emails matching the Find emails filters, one per turn: id, subject, from, from_name, to, received, unread, attachments, folder, or the whole email.

folder.description: Folder path: Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, or a folder below them, e.g. Inbox/Invoices.

subject_contains.description: Only emails whose subject contains this text.

from_contains.description: Only emails whose sender address or name contains this text.

received_after.description: Only emails received after this date and time.

with_body.description: Give each email whole: text, HTML, recipients and attachment names (one more request per email); the email stays unread. Without it each email has id, from, subject, received, unread and has_attachments.

mailbox.description: Another mailbox open in the runner's Outlook profile (its name or address), e.g. a shared mailbox; empty for the user's own.

received_before.description: Only emails received before this date and time (G3).

read_state.description: All emails, only unread ones or only read ones (G3); unread_only still works.

name: PDF
description: Extract text, merge, split, read and fill forms, encrypt, decrypt and convert PDF pages to images.

actions.name: Decrypt PDF
actions.description: Remove password protection (needs the open or owner password).

password.description: Password from the vault.

target.description: Unprotected PDF to create.

overwrite.description: Replace the target when it already exists; false stops with PDF.EXISTS.

actions.name: Encrypt PDF
actions.description: Protect a PDF with an open password and an owner password, choosing the AES key length and what readers may do (print, copy, edit, annotate, fill forms, assemble).

target.description: Encrypted PDF to create.

user_password.description: Password needed to open the PDF; anyone may open it when empty.

owner_password.description: Password needed to change permissions; a random one nobody knows when empty, so the permissions hold.

allow_assembly.description: Allow inserting, rotating and deleting pages.

allow_accessibility.description: Allow screen readers to extract the text.

key_length.description: AES key length in bits: 256 (recommended) or 128 for older readers.

overwrite.description: Replace the target when it already exists; false stops with PDF.EXISTS.

actions.name: Extract text from area
actions.description: Read the text inside a rectangle of one page, e.g. an invoice number box that is not a form field.

x.description: Left edge of the area in points (72 per inch) from the left of the page.

y.description: Top edge of the area in points from the top of the page.

width.description: Width of the area in points.

height.description: Height of the area in points.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

text.description: Text found inside the rectangle, trimmed.

actions.name: Extract fields by area
actions.description: Read the text of several named areas of a PDF at once, e.g. invoice number, date and total, into a Dictionary.

fields.description: Area name to {page, x, y, width, height}: points (72 per inch) from the top-left corner of the page; page 1 when left out.

trim.description: Remove spaces and line breaks around each value.

all_pages.description: Read each area on every page and give a List of values per name (for a form repeated page after page).

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

values.description: Each area's name and the text found in it (empty when nothing is there).

empty.description: Names of the areas where no text was found.

actions.name: Extract images
actions.description: Save the pictures embedded in a PDF (photos, logos, scanned pages), from every page or chosen pages, as image files in a folder.

min_size.description: Skip images narrower or lower than this many pixels (e.g. 32 to skip icons).

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

pages.description: Only pages listed here, e.g. 1,3,5-7; every page when empty.

file_prefix.description: Start of each image's file name, followed by _page1_img1 and so on; the PDF's name when empty.

color.description: Colour depth: color keeps the colours (24-bit); gray saves 8-bit greyscale copies; black_white saves 1-bit images.

dpi.description: Resize each image to this many dots per inch at the size it is shown on the page (e.g. a picture shown 2 inches wide becomes 300 pixels wide at 150 dpi); 0 keeps the pixels stored in the PDF. An image the page does not draw keeps its stored size.

jpeg_quality.description: JPEG quality from 1 (smallest file) to 100 (best picture); also used for TIFF with jpeg compression.

tiff_compression.description: TIFF compression: lzw and deflate are lossless; ccitt_g4 gives the smallest black-and-white files (images are made black and white); jpeg suits photos.

actions.name: Extract tables
actions.description: Find tables in a PDF that holds text (invoices, statements, reports) by how the text lines up in columns, and return each as a Data Table. Scanned PDFs need OCR first.

pages.description: Pages to read, e.g. 1,3-4; every page when empty.

header.description: The first row of each table holds the column names; Column1, Column2 … when off.

merge_across_pages.description: Join a table that continues at the top of the next page (same number of columns) into one, leaving out a repeated header row.

min_columns.description: Lines need at least this many separate columns to count as a table.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

tables.description: Every table found, as Data Tables, top to bottom and page by page.

table.description: The first (or only) table; an empty table when none was found.

actions.name: Extract text
actions.description: Extract the text of a PDF, of a page range or of chosen pages, as plain or layout-ordered text, optionally into a .txt file. Scanned PDFs (images) need OCR instead.

to_page.description: Last page; the end when empty.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

mode.description: structured orders text by its position on the page, keeping columns and tables readable; plain keeps the order stored in the file, like copy and paste.

pages.description: Exact pages to read, e.g. 1,3,5-7, in that order; overrides from_page and to_page.

output_file.description: Also write the text to this .txt file (UTF-8).

overwrite.description: Replace output_file when it already exists; false stops with PDF.EXISTS.

main.tick: Save the text to a file

actions.name: Fill form fields
actions.description: Fill form fields by name and save a new PDF; optionally flatten so values can no longer be edited.

values.description: Field name to value.

target.description: Filled PDF to create.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs; the filled copy is saved without protection.

actions.name: Get document properties
actions.description: Return the title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, dates, page count, PDF version and encryption of a PDF.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

include_custom.description: Also return custom document properties (any other keys in the document information) under custom, plus file_name.

properties.description: title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, created, modified, page_count, pdf_version, encrypted, and with include_custom also file_name and custom.

actions.name: Merge PDFs
actions.description: Combine several PDFs (a list, or every PDF in a folder), or chosen pages of each, in order, into one file; protected sources can be opened with passwords.

files.description: PDF paths in the order to merge.

target.description: Merged PDF to create.

overwrite.description: Replace the target when it already exists; false stops with PDF.EXISTS.

pages.description: Pages to take from each file, in the same order as files, e.g. ["1-3", "", "5,2"]; an empty entry takes every page.

passwords.description: Passwords (Credentials) for protected files, in the same order as files; empty entries for unprotected ones.

folder.description: Merge every PDF in this folder instead of a list, sorted by name (or by sort_by).

pattern.description: Which files of the folder, e.g. invoice-*.pdf.

sort_by.description: Order of the folder's files: by name or by last change (oldest first).

files.description: The PDFs that were merged, in order.

actions.name: Get page count
actions.description: Return the number of pages.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

actions.name: Read form fields
actions.description: Read the names and values of all form fields, or only of the fields named.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

field_names.description: Read only these fields, in this order; every field when empty. A name the form does not have stops the step.

fields.description: Field name to value.

actions.name: Read text with OCR
actions.description: Read the text of a scanned PDF (pages that are pictures, with no text layer) with Tesseract OCR, from every page or chosen pages, optionally keeping only the text between two markers.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

pages.description: Pages to read, e.g. 1,3,5-7; every page when empty.

language.description: Tesseract language(s), e.g. eng, deu or eng+fra.

page_mode.description: Page layout mode: 3 automatic, 6 single block, 7 single line, 11 sparse text.

dpi.description: Resolution the pages are rendered at for OCR; 300 suits most scans.

after_text.description: Keep only the text after the first occurrence of this marker, e.g. Invoice number:.

before_text.description: Keep only the text before this marker (searched after the after_text marker).

trim.description: Remove spaces and line breaks at the start and end of the result.

text.description: Recognised text of the pages, in page order.

pages.description: Recognised text of each page read, in page order.

more.tick: Keep only part of the text

actions.name: Read XPS text
actions.description: Read the text of an XPS or OpenXPS document (.xps, .oxps), page by page, in reading order.

text.description: The text of every page, pages separated by a blank line.

actions.name: Get page as picture
actions.description: Render one page as a PNG picture, returned as data (data: URI) with the page size in points; used by OneAgentStudio to draw an area to read, and to show a page in forms or emails.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

image.description: The page as a data:image/png;base64 URI.

width_points.description: Page width in points (72 per inch), as Extract text from area measures it.

page_count.description: Number of pages in the file.

actions.name: Split PDF
actions.description: Split a PDF into files of N pages each, into one file per page range, into one file holding chosen pages, at blank separator pages, or at its bookmarks.

pages_per_file.description: Pages in each part, for mode pages_per_file.

mode.description: pages_per_file cuts every N pages; ranges makes one file per comma-separated range in pages; selected_pages puts all pages listed in pages into one file; blank_page starts a new file after each blank page (blank pages are left out); bookmarks starts a new file at each bookmark down to bookmark_level.

pages.description: Page ranges for modes ranges and selected_pages.

file_prefix.description: Start of each part's file name, followed by _part1, _part2 and so on; the source file name when empty.

overwrite.description: Replace parts that already exist; false stops with PDF.EXISTS.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

bookmark_level.description: For mode bookmarks: the deepest bookmark level that starts a new file (1 = top-level bookmarks only, 2 = also their sub-bookmarks).

actions.name: Convert to images
actions.description: Save each page, or chosen pages, as an image (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF or TIFF) in colour, grey or black and white, for OCR or previews.

color.description: color keeps the colours; gray gives greyscale; black_white gives 1-bit images, often best for OCR.

pages.description: Pages to convert, e.g. 1,3,5-7; every page when empty.

file_prefix.description: Start of each image's file name, followed by _page1 and so on; the PDF's name when empty.

password.description: Password for protected PDFs.

jpeg_quality.description: JPEG quality from 1 (smallest file) to 100 (best picture); also used for TIFF with jpeg compression.

tiff_compression.description: TIFF compression: lzw and deflate are lossless; ccitt_g4 gives the smallest black-and-white files (pages are made black and white); jpeg suits photos.

name: PGP
description: Import keys, encrypt, decrypt, sign and verify files with OpenPGP: with GnuPG when it is installed on the runner, otherwise built in.

actions.name: Create key pair
actions.description: Generate a new OpenPGP key pair (signing key plus encryption subkey) and optionally export it to armored key files.

name.description: Key owner name (name, e-mail or both).

email.description: Key owner email address (name, e-mail or both).

passphrase.description: Passphrase that protects the private key; strongly recommended.

comment.description: Optional comment stored in the user id.

algorithm.description: Key type: ed25519 (modern, small) or RSA for older systems.

expires.description: Lifetime, e.g. 1y, 6m, 90d, a date like 2028-12-31, or never.

public_key_file.description: Where to save the armored public key (.asc) to share with partners.

private_key_file.description: Where to save the armored private key (.asc) as a backup; keep it secret.

gnupg_home.description: Separate key folder for this agent; the runner user's keyring when empty (GnuPG's, or the built-in one when GnuPG is not installed).

overwrite.description: Replace key files that are already there; when off, the step fails before any key is made.

user_id.description: User id stored in the key, e.g. Finance Agent <agent@example.com>.

actions.name: Decrypt file
actions.description: Decrypt a file with your private key.

target.description: Decrypted file to create; when empty, the encrypted file's name without .pgp, .gpg or .asc.

passphrase.description: Private key passphrase from the vault.

gnupg_home.description: Separate key folder for this agent; the runner user's keyring when empty (GnuPG's, or the built-in one when GnuPG is not installed).

private_key_file.description: Private key file (.asc or .gpg) to decrypt with, without importing it into a keyring first.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing target file.

target.description: Full path of the decrypted file.

actions.name: Encrypt file
actions.description: Encrypt a file for one or more recipients' public keys, or with a passphrase only (symmetric), choosing the cipher and compression.

target.description: Encrypted file to create; when empty, next to the file with .pgp added (.asc with armor), e.g. report.csv.pgp.

recipients.description: Recipient key ids, fingerprints or email addresses (text or List); may be empty when public_key_file is given.

gnupg_home.description: Separate key folder for this agent; the runner user's keyring when empty (GnuPG's, or the built-in one when GnuPG is not installed).

public_key_file.description: Recipient's public key file (.asc or .gpg) to encrypt for, without importing it into a keyring first.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing target file.

cipher.description: Symmetric cipher for the data; default lets GnuPG choose from the recipients' key preferences (AES-128 for a passphrase). Older ciphers (CAST5, 3DES, BLOWFISH) only for old partners.

compression.description: Compression before encryption; none for files that are already compressed, such as .zip or .jpg.

passphrase.description: Passphrase that can decrypt the file. Alone it gives passphrase-only (symmetric) encryption; with recipients either the keys or the passphrase can decrypt.

target.description: Full path of the encrypted file.

actions.name: Import key
actions.description: Import a public or private key file (.asc or .gpg).

passphrase.description: Passphrase, when importing a protected private key.

gnupg_home.description: Separate key folder for this agent; the runner user's keyring when empty (GnuPG's, or the built-in one when GnuPG is not installed).

actions.name: Sign file
actions.description: Create a detached signature (.sig) proving the file came from you.

signature.description: Signature file to create, e.g. report.csv.sig.

key.description: Signing key id or email; the default key when empty.

passphrase.description: Private key passphrase from the vault.

gnupg_home.description: Separate key folder for this agent; the runner user's keyring when empty (GnuPG's, or the built-in one when GnuPG is not installed).

actions.name: Verify signature
actions.description: Check a detached signature; returns the result instead of failing.

gnupg_home.description: Separate key folder for this agent; the runner user's keyring when empty (GnuPG's, or the built-in one when GnuPG is not installed).

valid.description: True when the signature is good.

name: PowerPoint
description: Open or create .pptx presentations, add, copy and delete slides, edit text, pictures and tables, and save.

actions.name: Add slide
actions.description: Add a slide with a chosen layout, optionally filling its title and body, at the end or at a given position.

layout.description: Slide layout from the first slide master that has it.

title.description: Text for the title placeholder.

body.description: Text for the body or subtitle placeholder; one line per bullet.

position.description: 1-based position for the new slide; at the end when empty.

actions.name: Close
actions.description: Close the presentation session, saving the changes first when asked.

save.description: Save the changes to the opened file before closing.

actions.name: Copy slide
actions.description: Duplicate a slide, including its text, pictures and tables, from this or another open presentation, and place the copy at a position.

slide.description: 1-based number of the slide to copy.

position.description: 1-based position for the copy; right after the original (or at the end, for another presentation) when empty.

session.description: Presentation session the copy goes into.

source_session.description: Session of another open presentation to copy the slide from; this presentation when empty.

actions.name: Create presentation
actions.description: Create a new .pptx (or .ppt or .odp) file on disk, empty or as a copy of a template presentation, optionally password-protected, and open it as a named session.

overwrite.description: Replace a file that already exists at the path.

session.description: Session name used by later steps.

password.description: Encrypt the new file with this password; later saves keep it.

template.description: Existing .pptx whose slide masters, layouts and slides the new file starts from; empty when empty.

edit_password.description: Password to modify: PowerPoint asks for it, or offers to open the file read-only.

main.tick: Require a password to open the file
Require a password to edit the file

actions.name: Delete slide
actions.description: Remove one slide, or several slides in a row, from the presentation.

count.description: How many slides to delete, starting at slide.

actions.name: Extract text from a file
actions.description: Return the whole text of a .ppt or .pptx file without opening it as a session, optionally with the speaker notes; old .ppt files included.

text.description: The presentation's text, slide after slide.

actions.name: Find and replace picture
actions.description: Swap pictures, found by alternative text or by their order across the slides, for a new image file, keeping the position and, unless a new size is given, the size.

alt_text.description: Replace every picture whose alternative text equals this.

index.description: 1-based position of the picture counting across all slides; used when alt_text is empty.

slide.description: Only look on this 1-based slide (index then counts on that slide); all slides when empty.

occurrence.description: With alt_text: replace all matching pictures, or only the first or last one in slide order.

new_alt_text.description: New alternative text for the replaced pictures; kept when empty.

width.description: New width in points; the current size is kept when width and height are empty.

keep_aspect_ratio.description: When only width or only height is given, scale the other side to the new image's proportions.

actions.name: Find and replace text
actions.description: Replace text on every slide, including tables and grouped shapes, e.g. fill {{name}} placeholders; can ignore case, match whole words or change only the first or last occurrence.

replace_with.description: Replacement text; empty removes what is found.

slide.description: Only this 1-based slide; all slides when empty.

whole_word.description: Only match the text as a whole word, not inside a longer word.

occurrence.description: Which occurrences to change, in slide order: all, the first or the last.

replace.description: G3 (AA parity): replace what is found (empty replacement removes it); when off the step only counts the matches (the default for new steps).

count.description: Number of matches found, or of replacements made.

actions.name: Format text
actions.description: Apply bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, size, colour or font to occurrences of a text on the slides; inputs left empty are not changed.

text.description: Text to format wherever it appears.

slide.description: Only this 1-based slide; all slides when empty.

whole_word.description: Only match the text as a whole word, not inside a longer word.

occurrence.description: Which occurrences to change, in slide order: all, the first or the last.

actions.name: Insert picture
actions.description: Place an image file on a slide at a position in points, optionally scaled to a width, a height or both.

slide.description: 1-based slide number; the current slide (the one added or copied last) when empty, else the last.

image.description: Image file (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, EMF or WMF).

x.description: Left edge in points.

width.description: Width in points; the height keeps the aspect ratio. Original size when empty.

alt_text.description: Alternative text, also used later by find_replace_picture.

height.description: Height in points; with width both are used as given, alone the width keeps the aspect ratio.

shape.description: Name of the new picture shape.

actions.name: Insert table
actions.description: Add a table to a slide from a Data Table, with the column names as an optional bold header row, at a position and size in points.

slide.description: 1-based slide number; the current slide (the one added or copied last) when empty, else the last.

x.description: Left edge in points.

include_header.description: Put the column names in a bold first row.

row_height.description: Height of each row in points; twice the font size when empty.

column_widths.description: Width of each column in points, in order; the total width is shared equally when empty.

height.description: G3 (AA parity): the whole table's height in points, shared by its rows (instead of a row height).

title.description: G3 (AA parity): the table's name, read by screen readers and shown in PowerPoint's selection pane.

shape.description: Name of the new table shape.

actions.name: Insert text
actions.description: Put text into a slide's title or body placeholder, or add it as a new text box at a position given in points.

slide.description: 1-based slide number; the current slide (the one added or copied last) when empty, else the last.

text.description: Text to insert; each line becomes a paragraph.

placeholder.description: title or body replaces that placeholder's text; none adds a new text box.

x.description: Text box left edge in points.

y.description: Text box top edge in points.

font_size.description: Font size in points for the new text.

bold.description: Bold on or off for the new text.

italic.description: Italic on or off for the new text.

underline.description: Underline on or off for the new text.

color.description: Hex colour for the new text.

font.description: Font name for the new text, e.g. Calibri.

alignment.description: Paragraph alignment of the new text; unchanged when empty.

actions.name: Open presentation
actions.description: Open a .pptx, .ppt or .odp presentation, or create a new empty one, as a named session; can open password-protected .pptx files and open read-only. .ppt and .odp files are converted with PowerPoint or LibreOffice on the runner and saved back in their own format.

create.description: Create the presentation when it does not exist.

session.description: Session name used by later steps.

read_only.description: Open for reading only: save over the opened file is refused, save_as to another file still works.

password.description: Password of an encrypted presentation; saves keep the file encrypted with it.

edit_password.description: Password to modify a presentation that has one; a wrong one stops the step. Without it such a file still opens (G3).

main.tick: The file has a password to edit

actions.name: Read text
actions.description: Return the text of every slide, one entry per slide in slide order.

slides.description: Text of each slide; shapes are separated by line breaks.

text.description: All slide texts joined, separated by blank lines.

actions.name: Save
actions.description: Save the presentation to the file it was opened from, or to another path; password-protected files stay protected.

path.description: Other path to write to; the opened file when empty.

password.description: Encrypt the saved file with this password; the password the presentation was opened with when empty.

actions.name: Save as
actions.description: Save the presentation to a new .pptx, .ppt or .odp file (.pptx optionally password-protected) and continue the session on that file, or export it as PDF.

format.description: pptx keeps the presentation; ppt (PowerPoint 97-2003) and odp are written with Microsoft PowerPoint (or LibreOffice) on the runner; pdf exports it the same way and the session stays on the previous file.

overwrite.description: Replace a file that already exists at the target path; false stops with PPT.EXISTS.

password.description: Encrypt the new file with this password; later saves keep it.

actions.name: Get slide count
actions.description: Count the slides in the presentation.

name: PowerPoint desktop
description: Insert videos and files, paste the clipboard and run macros using the installed Microsoft PowerPoint.

actions.name: Insert file
actions.description: Embed a file (an Excel sheet, a PDF, any file) on a slide as an icon that opens it when double-clicked in the slide show or editor.

file.description: File to embed.

label.description: Text under the icon; the file name when empty.

left.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

top.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

width.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

height.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

save.description: Save the presentation in place afterwards (when save_as is empty).

save_as.description: Save to this file instead of the opened one.

overwrite.description: Replace save_as when it exists; false stops with POWERPOINT_DESKTOP.EXISTS.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time.

shape.description: Name of the new shape on the slide.

position.description: left, top, width and height of the shape in points.

actions.name: Insert video
actions.description: Put a video (MP4, WMV, MOV …) on a slide, embedded in the presentation, at a position and size.

left.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

top.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

width.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

height.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

save.description: Save the presentation in place afterwards (when save_as is empty).

save_as.description: Save to this file instead of the opened one.

overwrite.description: Replace save_as when it exists; false stops with POWERPOINT_DESKTOP.EXISTS.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time.

shape.description: Name of the new shape on the slide.

position.description: left, top, width and height of the shape in points.

actions.name: Paste into slide
actions.description: Paste what is on the clipboard (a chart or range copied from Excel, a picture, text) onto a slide, optionally as a picture, and place it. PowerPoint only pastes into an open window, so a minimised PowerPoint window shows while it works.

paste_as.description: default pastes as PowerPoint would (a chart stays a chart); picture pastes a PNG picture of it; text pastes plain text.

left.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

top.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

width.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

height.description: In points (72 per inch) from the slide's top-left corner; PowerPoint's own when empty.

save.description: Save the presentation in place afterwards (when save_as is empty).

save_as.description: Save to this file instead of the opened one.

overwrite.description: Replace save_as when it exists; false stops with POWERPOINT_DESKTOP.EXISTS.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time.

shape.description: Name of the pasted shape on the slide.

position.description: left, top, width and height of the shape in points.

actions.name: Run macro
actions.description: Open a macro-enabled presentation, run a VBA macro with up to 5 text arguments, return its result and optionally save. A macro that stops with an error is reported straight away with its message.

macro.description: Macro name, optionally with its module.

arguments.description: Up to 5 arguments, passed to the macro as text.

save.description: Save the presentation in place afterwards (when save_as is empty).

save_as.description: Save to this file instead of the opened one.

overwrite.description: Replace save_as when it exists; false stops with POWERPOINT_DESKTOP.EXISTS.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time.

result.description: Value the macro returned (for a Function), as text; empty for a Sub.

description: List printers and print files.

printer.description: Default printer name, or empty when none is set.

actions.name: Get printers

printer.description: Printer name; default printer when empty.

confirm.description: Must be true to remove the printer.

name: REST Web Service
description: Call HTTP/REST APIs with JSON, headers and authentication.

actions.name: Download file
actions.description: Download a URL straight to a file (any file type, including large binaries), with the same headers and authentication as Send request.

url.description: Absolute URL of the file, or a path when base_url (or a connection) gives the address. It may come from the vault; then only its scheme and host are logged (G6).

path.description: File to save to, or a folder to keep the server's file name.

basic_password.description: Basic auth password from the vault.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file; off for new steps, so a file already there is not lost (G6).

timeout_seconds.description: Time allowed for the whole download.

insecure_tls.description: Accept any server certificate (self-signed or expired); for test systems only.

proxy.description: Proxy server as host:port; the runner's settings when empty.

proxy_user.description: Proxy user name, when the proxy needs a sign-in.

client_certificate.description: Client certificate (.p12 or .pfx) for servers that require mutual TLS.

client_certificate_password.description: Password of the client certificate file.

windows_auth.description: Windows sign-in (NTLM or Kerberos) for intranet sites, SharePoint on premises, IIS and Exchange: current_user signs in as the runner's Windows account (Windows runners); user_password uses basic_user (DOMAIN\user) and basic_password.

oauth_token_url.description: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint; the request is sent with a token fetched there (kept for the run and renewed before it expires).

oauth_client_secret.description: OAuth 2.0 client secret from the vault; needed for client credentials, optional with a refresh token.

oauth_refresh_token.description: Refresh token from the vault: signs in with the refresh-token grant instead of client credentials. A new refresh token from the server is used for the rest of the run and returned as refresh_token.

oauth_scope.description: Scopes to ask for, separated by spaces.

oauth_audience.description: Audience sent to the token endpoint (some providers, e.g. Auth0, need it).

oauth_resource.description: Resource sent to the token endpoint (e.g. Microsoft Entra v1 and AD FS).

oauth_client_auth.description: How the client id and secret reach the token endpoint: basic (HTTP Basic header, the OAuth standard) or body (form fields client_id and client_secret).

oauth1_consumer_key.description: OAuth 1.0a consumer key: the request is signed (RFC 5849).

oauth1_consumer_secret.description: OAuth 1.0a consumer secret from the vault.

oauth1_token.description: OAuth 1.0a access token from the vault; empty for a consumer-only (two-legged) request.

oauth1_token_secret.description: OAuth 1.0a token secret from the vault.

ntlm_user.description: Windows (NTLM) user name for intranet sites, IIS, SharePoint on premises and Exchange.

ntlm_domain.description: Windows domain of the NTLM user; empty when the user name already has it (DOMAIN\user or user@domain).

ntlm_password.description: Windows password of the NTLM user, from the vault.

base_url.description: Address the URL is relative to, so the URL can be a path such as /invoices/42; a saved connection usually gives it.

trust_certificate.description: Certificate of a private certificate authority (.cer, .crt or .pem) to trust as well as the usual ones, so a company server's certificate is still checked without insecure_tls (G6).

status.description: HTTP status code.

content_type.description: Content-Type reported by the server, or empty.
