name: Business rules
description: Decide with a decision table kept as a CSV file (or a table): conditions in in: columns, results in out: columns.

actions.name: Evaluate decision table
actions.description: Find the rules of a decision table that match the inputs and return what they give.

file.description: A CSV file with a header row of in:NAME, out:NAME and rule columns.

table.description: The decision table as a table value, with the same columns.

inputs.description: The values the in: columns test, by name.

default_outputs.description: What to give when no rule matches.

fail_when_none.description: Fail the step when no rule matches.

outputs.description: The out: values of the matching rule (first and unique); the first rule's for collect.

rule.description: The matching rule's name (its rule column, else its row number).

all.description: With collect: the outputs of every matching rule, in order.

name: Run context
description: Information about the current run: run id, runner, user and workspace.

actions.name: Get run information
actions.description: Return the run id, tenant, runner name, operating system user and working folder.

info.description: run_id, step_id, tenant, device, os_user, working_folder, os_name, os_version, java_version, processors, temp_folder.

actions.name: Get one run value
actions.description: Return a single item of the run information by name, e.g. run_id or device.

name: Salesforce
description: Query Salesforce with SOQL and create, read, update and delete records.

actions.name: Authenticate
actions.description: Get an access token from Salesforce with a connected app (client credentials, or user name and password) for the other Salesforce actions.

login_url.description: Login host for a custom sign-in site: your My Domain URL (needed for client credentials), or another login address.

grant_type.description: client_credentials: the connected app's run-as user; password: a named user with password and security token.

client_id.description: Consumer key of the connected app.

client_secret.description: Consumer secret from the vault.

username.description: User name (password grant only).

password.description: Password from the vault (password grant only).

security_token.description: Security token, added after the password, when the user's IP is not trusted (password grant only).

session.description: Keep this sign-in for the steps after it under this name; the toolkit's default session when empty (G6).

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same session (G6).

login_site.description: Where to sign in: production (login.salesforce.com), sandbox (test.salesforce.com) or custom (the login URL you give, such as your My Domain). When empty, the login URL is used (G6).

access_token.description: Access token; map it to access_token of later actions.

instance_url.description: Instance URL returned by Salesforce; map it to instance_url of later actions.

actions.name: Create record
actions.description: Create a record and return its id.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

fields.description: Field name to value.

api_version.description: REST API version.

id.description: New record id.

actions.name: Delete record
actions.description: Delete a record (it goes to the Salesforce recycle bin).

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

id.description: Record id.

api_version.description: REST API version.

actions.name: Describe object
actions.description: Read what an object has: its fields with their labels, types, lengths, whether they are required, picklist values and lookups.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

api_version.description: REST API version.

fields.description: Columns: name, label, type, length, required, updateable, picklist_values, reference_to.

object.description: name, label, label_plural, key_prefix, createable, updateable, deletable, custom.

actions.name: End session
actions.description: Forget the open Salesforce session; later steps then need their own address and sign-in (G6).

session.description: The session; the toolkit's default session when empty.

closed.description: True when a session was open.

actions.name: Find records
actions.description: Find records of an object whose fields have the values you give (each value quoted and escaped), without writing SOQL.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

conditions.description: Field to the value it must have; a list means any of them. Every condition must hold. Empty: every record.

fields.description: Fields to read, e.g. ["Id", "Name", "Email"]. Id and Name when empty.

order_by.description: A field to sort by, then ASC or DESC.

include_deleted.description: Also return deleted and archived records.

api_version.description: REST API version.

table.description: Records, one column per field asked for.

actions.name: Get attachments
actions.description: List the files and classic attachments on a record, or one file by its id, and optionally download them to a folder.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

record_id.description: Id of the record the files belong to. Not needed when content_document_id is filled in.

download_folder.description: Folder to save the files in; list only when empty.

api_version.description: REST API version.

kind.description: Only Salesforce Files (file), only classic attachments (attachment), or both.

name_pattern.description: Only files whose name matches this pattern (* and ?, case ignored); all when empty.

overwrite.description: Replace files of the same name in the folder; when off, a number is put in front of the new file's name.

content_document_id.description: Id of one Salesforce File (starts with 069): only that file is listed or downloaded, without a record id (G6).

extension.description: Only files with these extensions, separated by commas (with or without the dot, case ignored); all when empty (G6).

table.description: Columns: id, name, size, content_type, kind (file or attachment), path.

files.description: Paths of downloaded files (empty when not downloading).

path.description: Path of the first downloaded file, e.g. the one file asked for by content_document_id; empty when nothing was saved (G6).

actions.name: Get record
actions.description: Read one record by its Salesforce id, or by the value of an external id field.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

id.description: Record id, or the external id value when external_id_field is filled in.

fields.description: Fields to return; all when empty.

api_version.description: REST API version.

external_id_field.description: API name of an external id field; when filled in, the record whose field has the value in id is read.

actions.name: Query (SOQL)
actions.description: Run a SOQL query and return all matching records as a table (all result pages are read).

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

examples: SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Industry = 'Retail'

api_version.description: REST API version.

include_deleted.description: Also return deleted and archived records (queryAll).

batch_size.description: Records per page (200-2000); Salesforce's default when 0.

parameters.description: Values for :name in the SOQL, quoted and escaped for you, e.g. WHERE LastName = :name. A list becomes (a, b) for IN. Safer than putting values into the text.

total_size.description: Number of matching records Salesforce reports, which can be more than were read.

actions.name: Revoke authentication
actions.description: Revoke an access token so it can no longer be used.

access_token.description: The token to revoke.

actions.name: Save many records
actions.description: Write the rows of a Data Table as records, 200 a call (Salesforce's collections API), and get a result for each row.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

records.description: One row per record; the column names are the field API names (an Id column to update).

operation.description: Create: new records. Update: change the records in the Id column. Upsert: create or update by the external id field.

external_id_field.description: For upsert: the external id field that finds an existing record.

all_or_none.description: Write a call's records only if all of them can be written (otherwise the good ones are written and the others get an error).

api_version.description: REST API version.

results.description: One row per record: row (1, 2, ...), id, success, created, error.

actions.name: Update record
actions.description: Change fields of an existing record.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

id.description: Record id.

fields.description: Field name to new value.

api_version.description: REST API version.

actions.name: Upload attachment
actions.description: Upload a local file and link it to a record as a Salesforce File, or upload it as a new version of an existing file.

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

record_id.description: Id of the record to attach the file to. Not needed when content_document_id is filled in.

title.description: Title shown in Salesforce; the file name when empty.

api_version.description: REST API version.

visibility.description: Who can see the file on the record (AllUsers includes community users); Salesforce's default when empty, AllUsers for new steps. Not used for a new version, which keeps the file's sharing (G6).

content_document_id.description: Id of an existing file (starts with 069); the upload becomes its new version and keeps the file's links and sharing.

content_version_id.description: Id of the new file version.

content_document_id.description: Id of the file itself (filled when visibility or content_document_id is set).

actions.name: Upsert by external id

access_token.description: OAuth access token from the vault. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

object.description: Object API name.

external_id_field.description: API name of the external id field.

fields.description: Field name to value (do not repeat the external id field).

api_version.description: REST API version.

id.description: Record id (empty when Salesforce does not return it for an update).

created.description: True when a new record was created.

name: SAP GUI
description: Log on to SAP, run transactions, set and read fields, press buttons, read grids and the status bar through SAP GUI Scripting.

actions.name: Set check box
actions.description: Tick, clear or toggle a check box.

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

checked.description: True to tick, false to clear.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

toggle.description: Switch the check box to the opposite state; checked is then ignored.

actions.name: Click
actions.description: Click an element: buttons are pressed, tabs and radio buttons selected, check boxes toggled, other elements focused.

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

actions.name: Choose menu entry
actions.description: Choose an entry from the window's menu bar by its path of texts, e.g. System > User Profile > Own Data, by positions, or by its element id.

menu_path.description: Menu texts separated by > (or /), or a menu element id such as wnd[0]/mbar/menu[3]/menu[2].

window.description: Window number whose menu bar to use (0 = main window).

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

match_by.description: text: the path holds menu texts; index: it holds 0-based positions, e.g. 5 > 1 > 0.

actions.name: Close connection
actions.description: Log off and close an SAP connection.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

actions.name: Double-click
actions.description: Double-click an element, a grid cell or a tree node (fields get F2, which SAP treats as a double-click).

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

item.description: Grid row (0-based) or tree node key; empty for the current cell or a plain element.

column.description: Grid column (technical name, title or 0-based position).

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

actions.name: Expand tree node

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

match_by.description: Whether node_key is the node key, its displayed text, or its 0-based position among all nodes.

actions.name: Export table
actions.description: Read an ALV grid or a classic table control into a table, scrolling through all rows.

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

csv_path.description: Also save the rows to this CSV file; nothing is saved when empty.

encoding.description: Character encoding of the CSV file.

include_header.description: Write the column titles as the first CSV line.

append.description: Add to the end of an existing CSV file instead of replacing it (no header is added to a non-empty file).

table.description: Table content with the column titles as names.

path.description: The CSV file written, when csv_path was given.

main.tick: Save the rows to a CSV file

actions.name: Get check box or radio state

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

window.description: Window whose status bar to read (0 = main window).

type.description: S, W, E, I, A or empty.

column.description: Column: its position (from 1 or from 0, as set below), title, or technical field name.

actions.description: Find the first cell (or every cell) holding a value, ignoring surrounding spaces, and return its row and column.

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

column.description: Only search this column (position, title or field name); all columns when empty.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

case_sensitive.description: Match upper and lower case exactly.

all_occurrences.description: Keep searching and list every matching cell.

found.description: True when the value was found.

column.description: Column name (grid) or title (table control) of the match.

matches.description: Columns: row, column; every match when all_occurrences is on, else the first.

actions.name: Open system and log on

user.description: SAP user name; it may come from the vault.

language.description: Logon language.

system_type.description: Whether system is the SAP Logon entry description or a connection string such as /H/host/S/3200.

multiple_logon.description: What to do when SAP reports the user is already logged on: leave the question open, keep the other sessions, end them, or stop with an error.

logon_path.description: SAP Logon program to start first when it is not running; SAP Logon must already be open when empty.

start_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for SAP Logon to start.

connection.description: Connection number for later actions.

system_type.description: Whether system is the SAP Logon description or a connection string.

logon_path.description: SAP Logon program to start first when it is not running.

start_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for SAP Logon to start.

connection.description: Connection number for later actions.

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

fail_on_error_message.description: Stop with an error when the status bar then shows an error message.

actions.description: Press a button in the toolbar of an ALV grid or tree (e.g. &MB_EXPORT), optionally choosing an entry of its drop-down menu.

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

button_id.description: Button id as shown by the script recorder.

menu_item.description: Function code of the drop-down entry to choose; none when empty.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

actions.description: Read an ALV grid (GuiGridView) into a table, using the column titles as names.

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

technical_names.description: Name the columns by their technical field names (e.g. MATNR) instead of their titles.

actions.name: Right-click (context menu)

id.description: Scripting id from the SAP script recorder, e.g. wnd[0]/usr/ctxtVBAK-AUART.

item.description: Grid row (0-based) or tree node key.

column.description: Grid column (technical name, title or 0-based position).

menu_item.description: Entry to choose, as menu_by says: a function code (grids and trees) or element id (screen elements); the entry's text as shown; or its 0-based position, with sub-menus as 2 > 1.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

menu_by.description: How menu_item names the entry: code (function code or element id), text (the entry's text) or position (0-based, counted from the top).

value.description: Key, displayed text or 0-based position of the entry.

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

window.description: Window to send the key to (0 = main window, 1 = the first pop-up).

fail_on_error_message.description: Stop with an error when the status bar then shows an error message.

key.description: Key to press, by name; the number below is used when this is empty.

connection.description: SAP connection number (0 = first open system).

session.description: Session (window) number within the connection (0 = first).

press_enter.description: Press Enter in the window afterwards.

column.description: Column: its position (from 1 or from 0, as set below), title, or technical field name. With find_text, only this column is searched (all columns when empty).

row.description: Row of the cell that was changed (from 1 or from 0, as set).

name: SAP BAPI
description: Call SAP BAPIs and RFC function modules through SAP JCo: connect, run a function with imports, structures and tables, commit or roll back, read tables and function details.

actions.name: Run BAPI / function
actions.description: Run a BAPI or remote-enabled function module with import values (structures as dictionaries) and table rows; returns exports, tables, changing values and the RETURN messages. Fails on error messages (type E or A) unless told otherwise.

tables.description: Table parameters: name to a Table or a list of dictionaries (one per row).

commit.description: Run BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT (wait) right after a successful call.

fail_on_error.description: Stop with SAP_BAPI.FAILED when RETURN has an error (type E or A); the call is rolled back.

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

return_table.description: A table parameter to return on its own as Table.

return_structure.description: An export or changing structure to return on its own as a dictionary.

return_field.description: One value to return on its own: an export field, or STRUCTURE-FIELD.

table.description: With return_table: that table parameter after the call, on its own.

structure.description: With return_structure: that export or changing structure, on its own.

value.description: With return_field: that one value (an export field, or STRUCTURE-FIELD).

exports.description: Export parameters (structures as dictionaries, tables as Tables).

tables.description: Every table parameter after the call, as Tables.

messages.description: BAPI RETURN messages (type, id, number, message).

success.description: True when no RETURN message has type E or A.

actions.name: Commit
actions.description: Commit the work of the BAPIs called in this session (BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT), waiting for the update by default.

wait.description: Wait until the update is done (WAIT = X).

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Log on to an SAP system through SAP JCo (application server or message server with a logon group, optional SAP router and SNC) and keep the logon for the following steps.

host.description: Application server host name or IP address; it may come from the vault.

user.description: SAP user name; it may come from the vault.

password.description: SAP password from the vault.

language.description: Logon language, e.g. EN or DE.

message_server.description: Message server host, for load balancing instead of one application server; it may come from the vault.

system_id.description: Three-character system ID (with a message server).

snc_partner_name.description: SNC name of the SAP system; turns on SNC (secure, single sign-on).

snc_library.description: Path of the SNC library (e.g. sapcrypto.dll) when SNC is used.

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

sign_in.description: How to sign in: password (user and password), snc (secure network single sign-on), or snc_and_password (secure network plus user and password); worked out from the fields when empty.

snc_protection.description: SNC protection level: authentication only, integrity, privacy (encryption), the system's default, or the maximum both sides support.

gateway_host.description: Gateway host, when it is not the application or message server.

gateway_service.description: Gateway service (sapgwNN) or port, with the gateway host.

jco_folder.description: Folder holding sapjco3.jar and its native library, for this runner; the runner's usual places are used when empty.

system.description: system_id, client, user, host and release of the logon.

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: End the SAP logon of the session (uncommitted work is not saved).

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

actions.name: Get function details
actions.description: List the parameters of a BAPI or function module (direction, type, optional, description and the fields of structures and tables), to see what to fill in.

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

parameters.description: One dictionary per parameter: name, direction, type, optional, description, fields.

required_values.description: The imports, changing values and tables that must be given, with empty values to fill in (paste into Run BAPI / function).

actions.name: Read table
actions.description: Read rows of an SAP table or view with RFC_READ_TABLE: chosen fields, a WHERE condition in ABAP syntax and a row limit; values come back as text.

fields.description: Fields to read, e.g. ["MATNR", "MTART"]; all fields when empty (only for narrow tables).

where.description: WHERE condition in ABAP Open SQL syntax.

max_rows.description: Most rows to read (0 = no limit).

skip_rows.description: Rows to skip first, for reading in pages.

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

table.description: The rows read, one column per field.

actions.name: Roll back
actions.description: Undo the work of the BAPIs called in this session since the last commit (BAPI_TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK).

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

actions.name: Find functions
actions.description: Find remote-enabled functions and BAPIs by name pattern (* for any text) and function group, with their short descriptions.

pattern.description: Function name, with * for any text, e.g. BAPI_SALESORDER*.

group.description: Only functions of this function group (* allowed).

language.description: Language of the descriptions.

session.description: Session name; one SAP logon per session.

name: Scripts
description: Run PowerShell, Python, JavaScript and VBScript with arguments and captured output.

actions.name: Call function in session
actions.description: Call a function defined in an open script session with arguments, and return what it returns (G4).

session.description: Name of the script session, from Open script session.

function.description: Function name; dots for a function of an object or module.

arguments.description: Arguments in order.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time; the session is closed when it runs out.

fail_on_error.description: Stop the step when the function raises an error.

error.description: The error when fail_on_error is off; empty on success.

actions.name: Close script session
actions.description: End a script session and its program (G4); sessions also end with the run.

session.description: Name of the script session, from Open script session.

actions.name: Open script session
actions.description: Start Python, JavaScript (Node.js) or VBScript and keep it running for the steps after it: what one step defines is there for the next (G4).

language.description: The scripting language.

session.description: Session name the later steps use.

file.description: A script file to run first, e.g. one that defines functions.

interpreter.description: The program to use (python, node or cscript); found on the PATH when empty.

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same session.

actions.name: Run code in session
actions.description: Run code, or a file, in an open script session; the value of a last expression (Python, JavaScript) or of the code (VBScript Eval, when run_as is eval) comes back (G4).

session.description: Name of the script session, from Open script session.

file.description: Or a script file to run in the session.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time; the session is closed when it runs out.

fail_on_error.description: Stop the step when the code raises an error.

run_as.description: VBScript only: exec runs statements; eval works out an expression and returns its value.

result.description: The value of the last expression, when there is one.

error.description: The error when fail_on_error is off; empty on success.

actions.name: Run JavaScript
actions.description: Run JavaScript with Node.js, or with Windows' built-in JScript when Node.js is not installed.

file.description: Script file (or use script).

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the script, one list item each.

input.description: Text sent to the script's standard input (e.g. JSON).

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the exit code is not 0.

working_folder.description: Folder the script runs in; the workspace when empty.

environment.description: Extra environment variables for the script.

interpreter.description: Node.js program to use; node on the PATH when empty, and Windows' built-in JScript when Node.js is not installed.

json.description: Output parsed as JSON, when it is JSON.

actions.name: Run JavaScript function
actions.description: Call one function in a JavaScript file with Node.js (or Windows' built-in JScript when Node.js is not installed), passing JSON-compatible arguments, and return what it returns (promises are awaited with Node.js).

file.description: JavaScript file (.js) that defines or exports the function.

function.description: Function name; use object.method for a method of an exported object.

arguments.description: Arguments, in order.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum run time.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step when the function throws; when false the error is returned in error.

interpreter.description: Node.js program to use; node on the PATH when empty.

script.description: Code that defines the function, typed in the agent, instead of a file.

result.description: Value returned by the function (numbers, text, lists and dictionaries).

error.description: Error thrown by the function when fail_on_error is false; empty on success.

json.description: Output parsed as JSON, when it is JSON.

name: Snowflake
description: Run SQL in Snowflake, read results into data tables, browse databases, schemas and tables, and load rows.

actions.name: Run stored procedure
actions.description: Call a stored procedure with values for its arguments, sent apart from the SQL, and return what it gives back (G6).

procedure.description: Procedure name, written as DATABASE.SCHEMA.NAME (or just NAME).

parameters.description: Argument values: a list in the procedure's order, or a dictionary of argument name to value.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the procedure to finish.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database of the table when table_name has no database.

schema.description: Schema of the table when table_name has no schema.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

result.description: The value the procedure returned (the first cell of its result).

table.description: The whole result, for a procedure that returns a table.

actions.name: Cancel statement
actions.description: Stop a statement that is still running.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Keep the address and sign-in under a session for the steps after it, so they need not repeat them (G6).

account_url.description: The account url the later steps use (G6).

token.description: The token the later steps use (G6).

token_type.description: The token type the later steps use (G6).

session.description: The session's name; the toolkit's default session when empty.

share.description: Agents this one runs use the same session.

actions.name: Delete rows by key
actions.description: Delete the rows of a table whose key column has one of the values given; the values are sent apart from the SQL (G6).

table_name.description: Table, written as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (or just TABLE with database and schema set).

key_values.description: Key values of the rows to delete.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database of the table when table_name has no database.

schema.description: Schema of the table when table_name has no schema.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: Forget the open Snowflake session; later steps then need their own address and sign-in (G6).

session.description: The session; the toolkit's default session when empty.

closed.description: True when a session was open.

actions.name: Run SQL statement
actions.description: Run one SQL statement and return its rows as a data table. Use ? in the SQL for values passed in bindings.

sql.description: SQL to run. Put ? where each binding value goes.
examples: SELECT * FROM ORDERS WHERE REGION = ? AND AMOUNT > ?

bindings.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order, e.g. ["EMEA", 1000].

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database to use for names that are not fully written out.

schema.description: Schema to use for names that are not fully written out.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the statement to finish before returning with status running.

max_rows.description: Most rows to bring back into the table.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

table.description: Result rows (empty for statements that return no rows).

row_count.description: Number of rows in the table.

rows_affected.description: Rows inserted, updated or deleted by a data change.

statement_handle.description: Id of the statement, for status, results or cancel.

status.description: succeeded, or running when it did not finish within the wait time.

actions.name: Export results to file
actions.description: Run one SQL statement and write all of its rows to a file (CSV, tab-separated, JSON lines or Parquet), optionally compressed, without holding them all in memory.

sql.description: SQL to run. Put ? where each binding value goes.

file.description: File to write; add .gz yourself when compressing.

bindings.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order, e.g. ["2026-10-01"].

format.description: csv (comma-separated, quoted where needed), tsv (tab-separated), json_lines (one JSON object per row) or parquet (columnar, typed; G6).

header.description: Write the column names as the first line.

compression.description: none, or gzip to compress the file. For parquet: auto or snappy (snappy inside the file), gzip, or none. Auto on the other formats compresses with gzip when the file name ends with .gz (G6).

overwrite.description: Replace a file that already exists.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database to use for names that are not fully written out.

schema.description: Schema to use for names that are not fully written out.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the statement to finish.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

file.description: The file written.

actions.name: Get statement results
actions.description: Read the rows of a finished statement into a data table, page by page.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

row_count.description: Number of rows in the table.

total_rows.description: Rows in the full result, which can be more than max_rows.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

status.description: running, succeeded or failed.

message.description: Snowflake's message, including the error text when it failed.

total_rows.description: Rows in the result once it succeeded.

actions.description: Add every row of a data table to a Snowflake table. Columns are matched by name.

table_name.description: Target table, written as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (or just TABLE with database and schema set).

data.description: Rows to add. Its column names must match columns of the target table.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database of the table when table_name has no database.

schema.description: Schema of the table when table_name has no schema.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

table.description: One row per column with name, type, nullability and default.

table.description: One row per database with name, owner, comment and more.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

actions.name: List tables

schema.description: Schema to look in, e.g. PUBLIC.

table.description: One row per table with name, row count, size and more.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

actions.name: Load file into table
actions.description: Load a CSV or Parquet file into a table: a file on this machine is first put on the table's stage or a named stage, a file already on a stage is used as it is; then Snowflake copies it in (G6).

table_name.description: Table to load into, written as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (or just TABLE with database and schema set).

file.description: A CSV or Parquet file on this machine, or a path on a stage such as @MY_STAGE/orders/ (then nothing is uploaded).

stage.description: Named stage to put a local file on; the table's own stage when empty. The uploaded copy is removed once it is loaded.

format.description: csv (comma-separated, values may be in double quotes) or parquet (columns matched to the table's by name).

skip_header.description: Lines at the top of a CSV file that are not data, such as the column names.

on_error.description: On a bad row: abort (load nothing), continue (load the good rows), skip_file (leave out the file), or skip the file once it has on_error_limit bad rows or that percent of bad rows.

on_error_limit.description: The number of bad rows, or the percent of bad rows, after which a file is skipped.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for each statement to finish.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database of the table when table_name has no database.

schema.description: Schema of the table when table_name has no schema.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

errors_seen.description: Bad rows Snowflake found (skipped ones included).

results.description: Snowflake's result: one row per file with its status, rows loaded and first error.

actions.name: Update rows by key
actions.description: Set columns to new values in the rows of a table whose key column has one of the values given; the values are sent apart from the SQL (G6).

table_name.description: Table, written as DATABASE.SCHEMA.TABLE (or just TABLE with database and schema set).

key_values.description: Key values of the rows to update.

values.description: Column to its new value.

warehouse.description: Warehouse that runs the query. Leave empty for the user's default warehouse.

database.description: Database of the table when table_name has no database.

schema.description: Schema of the table when table_name has no schema.

role.description: Role to run as. Leave empty for the user's default role.

token.description: Access token from the vault: an OAuth token, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. Or leave it empty and choose a connection that signs in, which gets and renews the token.

token_type.description: Kind of token in the vault: OAUTH, KEYPAIR_JWT or PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

name: SOAP Web Service
description: Read a service's WSDL, call SOAP 1.1/1.2 web services and read the response as a dictionary.

actions.name: Read WSDL
actions.description: Read a service's WSDL (address or file) and list its operations, each with its SOAPAction, endpoint, SOAP version and a request body to fill in for Send SOAP request.

wsdl.description: The WSDL address, or a .wsdl file.

basic_user.description: Basic auth user name, when the WSDL needs a sign-in.

basic_password.description: Basic auth password from the vault.

timeout_seconds.description: Time to wait for each download.

insecure_tls.description: Accept any server certificate; for test systems only.

operations.description: Operations: name, soap_action, endpoint, version (1.1 or 1.2), style, body_template (? where a value goes).

main.tick: Sign in with a user name

actions.name: Send SOAP request
actions.description: Send a SOAP envelope (or just the body, which is wrapped for you), or build the request from the service's WSDL, and return the response.

url.description: Service endpoint URL, or a path when base_url (or a connection) gives the address. When the body is built from a WSDL, empty uses the address the WSDL gives.

body.description: Full SOAP envelope, or only the body XML (it is wrapped automatically); it may also come from the vault as a whole (G6).

soap_action.description: SOAPAction header (from the WSDL); when the body is built from a WSDL, empty uses the operation's own.

version.description: SOAP version; when the body is built from a WSDL, the port's own version is used.

basic_password.description: Basic auth password from the vault.

timeout_seconds.description: Response timeout.

insecure_tls.description: Accept any server certificate (self-signed or expired); for test systems only.

proxy.description: Proxy server as host:port; the runner's settings when empty.

proxy_user.description: Proxy user name, when the proxy needs a sign-in.

client_certificate.description: Client certificate (.p12 or .pfx) for servers that require mutual TLS.

client_certificate_password.description: Password of the client certificate file.

xpath.description: Also return the text of the response nodes this XPath selects, in values.

output_file.description: Also save the response XML to this file.

fail_on_error.description: Fail the step on a SOAP fault or HTTP error; when false the status and response are returned.

windows_auth.description: Windows sign-in (NTLM or Kerberos) for intranet sites, SharePoint on premises, IIS and Exchange: current_user signs in as the runner's Windows account (Windows runners); user_password uses basic_user (DOMAIN\user) and basic_password.

oauth_token_url.description: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint; the request is sent with a token fetched there (kept for the run and renewed before it expires).

oauth_client_secret.description: OAuth 2.0 client secret from the vault; needed for client credentials, optional with a refresh token.

oauth_refresh_token.description: Refresh token from the vault: signs in with the refresh-token grant instead of client credentials. A new refresh token from the server is used for the rest of the run and returned as refresh_token.

oauth_scope.description: Scopes to ask for, separated by spaces.

oauth_audience.description: Audience sent to the token endpoint (some providers, e.g. Auth0, need it).

oauth_resource.description: Resource sent to the token endpoint (e.g. Microsoft Entra v1 and AD FS).

oauth_client_auth.description: How the client id and secret reach the token endpoint: basic (HTTP Basic header, the OAuth standard) or body (form fields client_id and client_secret).

oauth1_consumer_key.description: OAuth 1.0a consumer key: the request is signed (RFC 5849).

oauth1_consumer_secret.description: OAuth 1.0a consumer secret from the vault.

oauth1_token.description: OAuth 1.0a access token from the vault; empty for a consumer-only (two-legged) request.

oauth1_token_secret.description: OAuth 1.0a token secret from the vault.

ntlm_user.description: Windows (NTLM) user name for intranet sites, IIS, SharePoint on premises and Exchange.

ntlm_domain.description: Windows domain of the NTLM user; empty when the user name already has it (DOMAIN\user or user@domain).

ntlm_password.description: Windows password of the NTLM user, from the vault.

base_url.description: Address the URL is relative to, so the URL can be a path such as /invoices/42; a saved connection usually gives it.

wsdl.description: Build the request from this WSDL (address or .wsdl file) instead of writing the XML (G6).

service.description: Service in the WSDL; empty when it has only one or any will do (G6).

port.description: Port of the service (it fixes the address and SOAP version); empty for the first that offers the operation (G6).

operation.description: Operation to call, as Read WSDL lists it (G6).

parameters.description: Values of the request's fields: field name (or a path such as Customer/Name) to value; a value may be a Credential, and a list repeats the field. Optional fields left out are dropped (G6).

namespace.description: Namespace for the operation's element in place of the WSDL's (G6).

qualify_elements.description: Whether the fields inside the operation carry the namespace too; empty follows the WSDL's schema (G6).

replace_in_body.description: Placeholders in the body filled just before sending: name to a Credential (or text); every {{name}} in the body becomes the value, which stays masked in the log (G6).

xpath_output.description: What xpath returns: values (a list of the nodes' text), joined (their text as one text, separated by delimiter), inner_xml (the XML inside the nodes) or outer_xml (the nodes with their own tags) (G6).

delimiter.description: What separates the joined values: none, pipe (|), semicolon (;) or custom (G6).

custom_delimiter.description: Text that separates the joined values (G6).

trust_certificate.description: Certificate of a private certificate authority (.cer, .crt or .pem) to trust as well as the usual ones, so a company server's certificate is still checked without insecure_tls (G6).

status.description: HTTP status code.

body.description: The first element inside the SOAP Body, as a dictionary.

values.description: Text of the nodes selected by xpath (their inner or outer XML with those xpath_output choices); empty without xpath.

text.description: With xpath_output joined, inner_xml or outer_xml: the selected nodes as one text; empty otherwise (G6).

options.label: Windows user name and password, NTLM

name: Play sound
description: Beep, play a WAV file, or play MP3, WMA, M4A and video files, e.g. to alert an attended user.

actions.name: Beep
actions.description: Play the system beep, once or several times.

actions.name: Play sound file
actions.description: Play a WAV, AIFF or AU sound file, waiting until it ends or continuing while it plays.

wait.description: Wait until the sound has finished; false continues while it plays.

volume_percent.description: Playback volume from 1 to 100 percent of the file's level.

repeat.description: How many times to play the sound (1 to 20).

actions.name: Play media file
actions.description: Play an MP3, WMA, M4A, WAV or other audio file, or a video (MP4, WMV, AVI...) in a window, with the media support of Windows; wait until it ends or continue while it plays.

path.description: Audio or video file, e.g. C:\alerts\done.mp3.

show_video.description: Show the picture in a window (for video files); audio files then show an empty window. Esc closes it.

wait.description: Wait until playing has finished; false continues while it plays (Stop media ends it).

repeat.description: How many times to play the file.

max_seconds.description: Stop after this many seconds; 0 plays to the end.

window_width.description: Width of the video window in pixels.

window_height.description: Height of the video window in pixels.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the media in seconds (0 when not known, e.g. when not waiting).

actions.name: Stop media
actions.description: Stop media files started by Play media file without waiting.

name: String
description: Text manipulation: extract, replace, split, join, clean, mask, fill templates, encode and change case.

actions.name: Change case
actions.description: Convert text to upper, lower, title or sentence case, or to camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case or kebab-case for names and keys.

case.description: Target case: camel is invoiceTotal, pascal InvoiceTotal, snake invoice_total, kebab invoice-total.

actions.name: Compare
actions.description: Compare two texts exactly, ignoring case, or in natural order where numbers inside the text are compared by value.

mode.description: exact, ignore_case, or natural (file2 before file10, case ignored).

ignore_line_breaks.description: Treat each line break (\r\n or \n) as a space, so text wrapped onto several lines still matches.

result.description: -1 when the first text comes first, 0 when they are equal, 1 when it comes after.

equal.description: True when the texts are equal under the chosen mode.

actions.name: Count occurrences
actions.description: Count how many times a piece of text appears in a text (matches do not overlap).

match_case.description: Count only matches with the same upper and lower case.

whole_word.description: Count only matches that are whole words, not parts of longer words (cat in cat food, not in catalogue).

count.description: Number of times it appears; 0 when it does not.

actions.name: Count words and lines
actions.description: How many words, lines, sentences and characters a text has.

lines.description: Lines, empty ones included; 0 for empty text.

characters_no_spaces.description: Characters without spaces and line breaks.

actions.name: Encode or decode text
actions.description: Make text safe for, or read it back from, a web address (URL), HTML, XML, JSON or Base64.

format.description: URL: a value in a web address (a space is %20); HTML and XML: < > & and quotes; JSON: the inside of a JSON text (quotes, \n); Base64: UTF-8 bytes.

actions.name: Escape for regex
actions.description: Put a backslash before every character that has a meaning in regular expressions, so the text is matched exactly, e.g. 1+1=2? to 1\+1=2\?.

result.description: The text, safe to use inside a regular expression.

actions.name: Extract with pattern
actions.description: Take the parts of a text a pattern describes, e.g. the date, number and amount of "Invoice 42 of 2026-11-16: 99.50"; named parts come back as a Dictionary.

pattern.description: A regular expression with bracket groups, named like (?<total>[\d.]+) if you want them by name.

occurrence.description: Which match to take: 1 for the first.

found.description: True when the pattern was found.

named.description: Each named group (?<name>...) by its name.

actions.name: Extract text
actions.description: Return the text before, after or between markers.

after_occurrence.description: Which occurrence of the 'after' marker to start from (1 = first).

before_occurrence.description: Which occurrence of the 'before' marker to stop at (1 = first).

ignore_case.description: Find the markers without regard to upper/lower case.

if_not_found.description: Result when a marker is missing: empty text, or the whole source text.

max_length.description: Keep at most this many characters of the result.

remove_line_breaks.description: Remove line breaks from the result.

until.description: Where the result ends when the 'before' marker is empty or not found: as before (marker), at the end of the line, or at the end of the text.

markers.description: G1 (AA parity): with both markers given, whether either one found is enough, or both must be found (else the marker is missing).

length_mode.description: G1 (AA parity): keep up to max_length characters, or exactly that many (a shorter result counts as not found).

result.description: Extracted text, empty when a marker is missing.

actions.name: Fill a template
actions.description: Put values into a text with {name} places, e.g. "Dear {first_name}, invoice {number} is due on {due}." from a Dictionary or a table row.

template.description: Text with places in curly brackets, e.g. {name}; {{ and }} write a bracket.

values.description: The values by name: a Dictionary or a table row (a Record).

if_missing.description: A place without a value: keep {name}, leave it empty, or fail with STRING.MISSING_VALUE.

from_agent.description: G1 (AA parity): also fill $name$ places with the agent's own variables now, for a text read while the agent runs (from a file or a web page). Credentials are never filled in.

actions.name: Find
actions.description: Find where a text (or regular expression) first appears, starting from a position.

find.description: Text or regular expression to look for.

start.description: Zero-based position to start searching from.

occurrence.description: Which match to return (1 = first, 2 = second ...).

group.description: Regular expression: return this capture group in match and all_matches instead of the whole match, e.g. 1 for the number in Total: (\d+).

index.description: Zero-based position of the match, or -1 when not found.

found.description: True when a match was found.

match.description: The matched text (or the chosen group), empty when not found.

position.description: One-based position of the match, or 0 when not found.

groups.description: Regular expression: the capture groups of the returned match (group 1 first); empty otherwise.

named_groups.description: Regular expression: named groups (?<name>...) of the returned match.

all_matches.description: Every match from the start position on, in order.

count.description: How many matches there are from the start position on.

actions.name: Find all matches
actions.description: Every place a text or pattern occurs, as a list: all invoice numbers, e-mail addresses or amounts in a text.

group.description: Keep this bracket group of each match; 0 keeps the whole match.

actions.name: Insert text
actions.description: Put text into another text at a position (counted from 0), at the start or at the end.

position.description: Where it goes, counted from 0; -1 puts it at the end.

actions.name: Join texts
actions.description: Join the items of a list into one text with a separator, e.g. names into Ann, Bo and Cy, leaving out empty items if you like.

items.description: The texts, as a List variable or ["a", "b"]; numbers and dates are written as text.

separator.description: Put between items; a line break is \n.

last_separator.description: Put before the last item instead, e.g. " and ".

actions.name: Get length
actions.description: Count the characters in a text.

actions.name: Mask text
actions.description: Hide most of a text behind a character, keeping the first or last few, e.g. a card number as ************1111 or an e-mail as a***@example.com.

keep_last.description: Characters to keep visible at the end.

keep_first.description: Characters to keep visible at the start.

mask_character.description: The character that hides the rest.

keep_separators.description: Leave spaces, dashes and dots as they are (4111 1111 1111 1111 becomes **** **** **** 1111).

email.description: Mask only the part before the @, keeping its first character.

actions.name: Normalize spaces
actions.description: Turn runs of spaces, tabs and no-break spaces into one space and trim the ends, keeping or joining the lines, e.g. for text read from web pages or PDFs.

keep_line_breaks.description: Keep the lines (tidying each, and dropping empty ones); when off, everything becomes one line.

actions.name: Pad text
actions.description: Fill a text up to a length with a character on the left or the right, e.g. 42 to 00042; longer text is left as it is.

text.description: Source text; a number is used as it is written, e.g. 42.

length.description: Length the result should have, in characters.

character.description: One character to fill with; a space when empty.

side.description: left puts the fill before the text (numbers, codes); right puts it after (fixed-width columns).

actions.name: Random text
actions.description: Generate random text of a given length from letters, digits and/or symbols.

letter_case.description: Letters in mixed, upper or lower case.

exclude_characters.description: Characters never to use, e.g. 0O1l to avoid look-alikes.

actions.name: Remove characters
actions.description: Strip digits, letters, punctuation, spaces, line breaks or accents (é becomes e), or characters you list, e.g. to clean phone numbers or IDs.

punctuation.description: Remove punctuation and symbols such as . , - ( ) / # @.

accents.description: Keep the letters but drop their accents: café becomes cafe, Müller becomes Muller.

characters.description: Any other characters to remove, typed one after another, e.g. $€£.

keep_instead.description: Keep only the ticked kinds and listed characters, removing everything else (e.g. tick Digits to keep only digits).

actions.name: Remove part of text
actions.description: Cut out a number of characters from a position (counted from 0), e.g. a prefix or a check digit.

start.description: First character to remove, counted from 0.

length.description: How many characters; to the end when empty.

actions.name: Repeat text
actions.description: Repeat a text a number of times, with a separator between, e.g. a line of dashes or placeholders.

actions.name: Replace
actions.description: Replace text, optionally using a regular expression.

ignore_case.description: Match without regard to upper/lower case.

start.description: Zero-based position to start replacing from; text before it is kept as is.

count.description: Replace at most this many matches; -1 replaces all.

actions.name: Reverse
actions.description: Return the text with its characters in reverse order.

actions.name: Shorten text
actions.description: Cut a text to a maximum length and add an ending such as …, if you like at a word break, e.g. for subjects, columns or messages.

ending.description: Added when the text is cut; empty adds nothing.

whole_words.description: Cut at the last space rather than in a word.

result.description: The shortened text (unchanged when it was short enough).

shortened.description: True when the text was cut.

actions.name: Split
actions.description: Split text into a list by a delimiter.

max_parts.description: Split into at most this many parts; the last part keeps the rest. 0 splits at every delimiter.

ignore_case.description: Match a letter delimiter without regard to upper/lower case.

regex.description: Treat the delimiter as a regular expression, e.g. \R for any line break.

actions.name: Get part of text
actions.description: Return the part of a text from a start position, for a length or up to an end position.

length.description: Number of characters to take; to the end when empty.

end.description: Zero-based end position (not included); used when length is empty.

if_out_of_range.description: When the start is past the end of the text: fail with STRING.BAD_POSITION, or return empty text.

result.description: The selected part of the text.

actions.name: Number to locale text
actions.description: Write a number as text using the separators of a locale, e.g. 1.234,5 for de-DE.

decimals.description: Fixed decimal places; keeps the number's own decimals when empty.

actions.name: Text to number
actions.description: Read a number from text written for a locale, or with the decimal and grouping separators you give.

locale.description: Locale the text is written in, e.g. en-US, de-DE, fr-FR.

ignore_currency.description: Ignore a currency symbol or code before or after the number ($, €, ₹, USD, EUR, Rs.); when off such text is not a number.

actions.name: Trim
actions.description: Remove spaces, or the characters you list, from both ends, the start or the end of a text.

characters.description: Characters to remove, e.g. 0 or *-; whitespace when empty.

conditions.name: Text contains
conditions.description: True when the text has the other text in it, anywhere or as a whole word.

whole_word.description: Only as a whole word (urgent, not urgently).

conditions.name: Text ends with
conditions.description: True when the text finishes with the other text.

end.description: The ending to look for, e.g. .pdf.

conditions.name: Text is an email address
conditions.description: True when the text looks like an email address.

conditions.name: Text is empty
conditions.description: True when the text has no characters (or, if you like, only spaces).

text.description: Text to check; an empty variable counts as empty.

spaces_are_empty.description: Text of only spaces, tabs and line breaks counts as empty.

conditions.name: Text is a number
conditions.description: True when the text is a number, e.g. 1,250.50 or -3.

conditions.name: Text matches a pattern
conditions.description: True when the text fits a regular expression, as a whole or somewhere in it, e.g. ^INV-\d{6}$ for an invoice number.

pattern.description: The regular expression.

whole_text.description: The whole text must fit; when off, a match anywhere counts.

conditions.name: Text starts with
conditions.description: True when the text begins with the other text.

name: System
description: Read environment variables and runner information; lock, sign out, restart or shut down the runner.

actions.name: Delete environment variable
actions.description: Remove an environment variable for programs this run starts (process scope) or permanently for the runner's user (user scope, Windows).

scope.description: process: programs and scripts started later in this run; user: removed for the runner's Windows user.

actions.name: Empty recycle bin
actions.description: Delete everything in the recycle bin of one drive or of every drive. This cannot be undone.

confirm.description: Must be true to empty the recycle bin.

drive.description: Drive letter; every drive when empty.

count.description: Number of items that were in the recycle bin.

actions.name: Get environment variable
actions.description: Read an environment variable of the runner; variables that look like secrets are refused.

default.description: Value when the variable is not set.

value.description: Value, or the default when not set.

actions.name: List environment variables
actions.description: Return every environment variable of the runner as a dictionary; variables that look like secrets are left out.

variables.description: Variable name to value, sorted by name.

hidden_count.description: How many secret-looking variables were left out.

actions.name: Get screen resolution
actions.description: Return the resolution and display scaling of the main screen, and of every screen.

width.description: Main screen width in pixels, e.g. 1920.

height.description: Main screen height in pixels, e.g. 1080.

screens.description: Every screen: width, height, scale_percent, refresh_hz, primary.

actions.name: Get system info
actions.description: Return the runner name, operating system, user, processors and Java version.

info.description: hostname, os, os_version, user, processors, java_version.

actions.name: List processes
actions.description: List the running programs with their process id, memory use, start time and window title, optionally only those whose name contains a text.

name_contains.description: Only processes whose name contains this text (any case); all when empty.

with_window_only.description: Only processes that show a window.

processes.description: Records with name, pid, memory_mb, started (UTC) and window_title, sorted by name.

actions.name: Lock computer
actions.description: Lock the screen of the current session.

actions.name: Sign out
actions.description: Sign out the current Windows user (open programs are closed).

confirm.description: Must be true to sign out.

force.description: Close programs without asking them to save (unsaved work is lost).

actions.name: Desktop notification
actions.description: Show a Windows notification with a title and a message to the person signed in on the runner; the agent does not wait.

title.description: Title in bold.

message.description: Text under the title.

actions.name: Restart computer
actions.description: Restart the runner after a delay.

force.description: Close programs without asking them to save (unsaved work is lost).

message.description: Reason shown to signed-in users and written to the Windows event log.

actions.name: Set environment variable
actions.description: Set an environment variable for programs this run starts (process scope) or permanently for the runner's user (user scope, Windows).

name.description: Variable name: letters, digits and underscores.

scope.description: process: programs and scripts started later in this run; user: saved for the runner's Windows user.

actions.name: Set screen resolution
actions.description: Change the main screen's resolution for this Windows session (not saved), for agents that need a fixed screen size; put back when the run ends unless turned off.

confirm.description: Must be true to change the screen.

refresh_hz.description: Refresh rate, e.g. 60; the screen's choice when empty.

restore_at_end.description: Put the saved resolution back when the run ends (also when it fails).

actions.name: Show desktop
actions.description: Minimise every window so the desktop shows, like Windows+D.

actions.name: Shut down computer
actions.description: Shut the runner down after a delay.

confirm.description: Must be true to shut down.

force.description: Close programs without asking them to save (unsaved work is lost).

message.description: Reason shown to signed-in users and written to the Windows event log.

name: Terminal emulator
description: Connect to IBM mainframe 3270 screens, IBM i (AS/400) 5250 screens or VT100/ANSI hosts over SSH, type into fields, press Enter and function keys, and read screen text. 3270 needs the free wc3270 engine on the runner (wc3270 installer); 5250 and SSH need nothing.

actions.name: Clear screen
actions.description: Erase all input fields locally, or send the Clear key to the host.

send_to_host.description: Send the Clear key to the host (blanks the whole screen) instead of only erasing input fields.

actions.name: Connect
actions.description: Connect to a TN3270 or TN5250 host, or sign in to a VT100/ANSI host over SSH, and wait for the first screen. 3270 needs the free wc3270 engine installed on the runner; 5250 and SSH need nothing.

host.description: Host name or address; it may come from the vault (G4).

port.description: Port; 23 for 3270 and 5250 (992 is common with TLS) and 22 for SSH when empty.

model.description: Screen model. 3270: 2 = 24x80, 3 = 32x80, 4 = 43x80, 5 = 27x132; 3278 is monochrome; -E adds the extended attributes (colour, highlighting). 5250: 3477-FC and 3477-FG are 27x132, the others 24x80 (a 3270 model 5 also means 27x132).

terminal_type.description: tn3270e (extended 3270, the usual mainframe choice), plain tn3270 for hosts that refuse the extensions, tn5250 for IBM i (AS/400) hosts, vt-ssh for a VT100/ANSI host reached over SSH, or vt-telnet for one reached over Telnet (unencrypted) (G4).

connect_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the connection and the first screen.

lu_name.description: Device name to request from the host (3270 logical unit, or 5250 display device); any free one when empty.

code_page.description: Host code page, e.g. cp037 (US), cp273 (German), cp500; the engine default (5250: cp037) when empty.

wait_for_input_field.description: Wait until the first screen has a field to type into (on SSH: until the host stops sending); turn off for hosts that show a read-only banner first.

wait_for_text.description: Text the first screen must show (e.g. a logon prompt) before the agent continues; no check when empty.

user.description: SSH user name; over Telnet, typed at the login prompt (empty: sign in with Type text steps). It may come from the vault.

password.description: Password from the vault; over SSH leave it empty when signing in with a key file.

key_file.description: Private key file for SSH sign-in (instead of, or as well as, a password).

key_passphrase.description: Passphrase of the key file, when it has one.

host_key_fingerprint.description: Expected SSH host fingerprint; the connection stops when the host shows a different one. Strongly recommended.

emulation.description: Terminal kind reported to the SSH host; it decides which control codes the host sends.

screen_rows.description: Screen height in rows for SSH hosts.

screen_columns.description: Screen width in columns for SSH hosts.

encoding.description: VT hosts: how characters are sent: utf-8, ansi (windows-1252), or a double-byte set such as Shift_JIS, GBK or EUC-KR (G4).

auto_wrap.description: VT hosts: text reaching the right edge goes on at the next line; off keeps writing in the last column (G4).

device_attributes.description: VT hosts: the answer to the host's 'what terminal are you' question, after ESC [ (e.g. ?62;1;6c for a VT220); the VT100 answer when empty (G4).

main.tick: Sign in with a key file
Ask for a specific device name
Wait for text on the first screen

actions.name: Disconnect
actions.description: Disconnect and close the terminal.

actions.name: Get all fields
actions.description: List every field on the screen with its position, length, protection and text.

table.description: Columns: index, row, column, length, protected, numeric, hidden, text.

actions.name: Get cursor position
actions.description: Read the row and column where the cursor is.

column.description: Cursor column (1-based).

actions.name: Get field
actions.description: Read one field, found by a screen position inside it or by the label just before it.

row.description: Row of any position in the field (1-based).

column.description: Column of that position (1-based).

label.description: Label text shown before the field; used instead of row and column.

index.description: Field number as listed by Get all fields, counted from 1 (add 1 to a number counted from 0); used instead of position or label.

text.description: Field text (trimmed; empty for hidden fields).

field.description: index, row, column, length, protected, numeric, hidden, text.

actions.name: Get screen text
actions.description: Read the whole screen as text, one line per row.

trim_lines.description: Remove trailing spaces from each row.

to_row.description: Last row to return; 0 for the bottom of the screen.

actions.name: Get text at position
actions.description: Read text from a row and column for a given length, or the last line with text, a rectangle of the screen, or (VT hosts) everything that scrolled past.

column.description: Column (1-based).

what.description: What to read (G4): from a position, a rectangle (row, column, height, width), the last line with text, or on VT hosts all lines that scrolled off the top and the screen.

text.description: Text (trimmed unless trim is off); a rectangle or the scroll-back one line per row.

actions.name: Hide terminal
actions.description: Close the window Show terminal opened (G4); the session goes on.

actions.name: Find text on screen
actions.description: Find where a piece of text appears on the screen.

occurrence.description: Which match to return when the text appears more than once.

case_sensitive.description: Match upper and lower case exactly.

whole_field.description: Only match a field whose whole (trimmed) text equals the search text.

found.description: True when the text was found.

row.description: Row of the first character (0 when not found).

column.description: Column of the first character (0 when not found).

field_index.description: Number of the field holding the match, as in Get all fields (0 when not found or the screen has no fields).

count.description: How many times the text appears on the screen.

actions.name: Press key
actions.description: Press Enter, Tab, Clear, a PF or PA key, and wait for the host to answer.

key.description: Enter, Tab, BackTab, Clear, Reset, EraseEOF, EraseInput, Home, Newline, Up, Down, Left, Right, BackSpace, Delete, Insert, FieldEnd, Dup, FieldMark, Attn, SysReq, PF1 to PF24 or PA1 to PA3. 5250 (IBM i) hosts also take FieldExit, Help, Print, PageUp and PageDown (Roll Down and Roll Up), but not PA keys or FieldMark. VT (SSH) hosts also take Escape, End, PageUp, PageDown and Ctrl+letter, e.g. Ctrl+C.

wait_for_host.description: After keys that go to the host (Enter, PF, PA, Clear...), wait until it unlocks the keyboard.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the host to unlock the keyboard after the key.

repeat.description: How many times to press the key, e.g. 3 x Tab.

delay_after_ms.description: Extra pause after the key, in milliseconds.

wait_for_text.description: Text that must appear on the screen after the key (waits up to timeout_seconds); no check when empty.

actions.name: Type text
actions.description: Type text at a row and column, or at the cursor; Credentials are typed without being logged.

text.description: Text, or a Credential variable for passwords.

row.description: Row (1-based); the cursor position when empty. On VT (SSH) hosts the cursor is moved with arrow keys, which suits full-screen programs.

column.description: Column (1-based).

clear_field.description: Erase the rest of the field first.

press_key.description: Key to press after typing, e.g. Enter or PF8; none when empty.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the host to unlock the keyboard after the key.

delay_after_ms.description: Extra pause after typing (and the key), in milliseconds.

wait_for_text.description: Text that must appear on the screen afterwards (waits up to timeout_seconds); no check when empty.

delay_before_ms.description: Pause before typing, e.g. for a slow host (G4).

actions.name: Set cursor
actions.description: Move the cursor to a row and column.

column.description: Column (1-based).

actions.name: Set field
actions.description: Replace the contents of an input field, found by position, label or field number; Credentials are typed without being logged.

text.description: Text, or a Credential variable for passwords.

row.description: Row of any position in the field (1-based).

column.description: Column of that position (1-based).

label.description: Label text shown before the field; the next input field after it is used.

index.description: Field number as listed by Get all fields, counted from 1 (add 1 to a number counted from 0); used instead of position or label.

press_key.description: Key to press after filling the field; none when empty.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the host to unlock the keyboard after the key.

wait_for_text.description: Text that must appear on the screen afterwards, e.g. the next screen's title (waits up to timeout_seconds); no check when empty.

actions.name: Set key mapping
actions.description: Give keys friendly names for this session, e.g. Submit for Enter or Exit for PF3, usable in Press key.

mappings.description: Name to key, e.g. {"Submit": "Enter"}; an empty key removes the name.
All names set in this session.

actions.name: Show terminal
actions.description: Open a window that follows the session's screen while the agent works, for a person watching (G4); on a runner without a screen it only notes that in the log.

shown.description: True when the window is showing.

actions.name: Wait for screen
actions.description: Wait until the host unlocks the keyboard, shows an input field, changes the screen, or a number of seconds passes.

condition.description: input_field: a typeable field is shown; unlock: keyboard unlocked (terminal ready); screen_change: the host sends new output; screen_blank: the screen is empty; cursor_at / cursor_leaves: the cursor reaches or leaves row and column; seconds: just pause.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wait (the pause length for seconds).

fail_on_timeout.description: Stop with an error on timeout; when off, met is false instead.

column.description: Column (1-based) for cursor_at and cursor_leaves.

met.description: True when the condition was met in time (false only when fail_on_timeout is off).

actions.name: Wait for prompt
actions.description: On VT (SSH) hosts: wait until the host has finished writing and the cursor sits after a prompt such as $, # or >, e.g. after a command.

prompt.description: Regular expression the text before the cursor must end with; a shell prompt ($, #, >, %) when empty.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wait.

quiet_ms.description: The screen must stay unchanged this long, so a prompt-like character in the middle of output does not count.

fail_on_timeout.description: Stop with an error on timeout; when off, found is false instead.

found.description: True when the prompt appeared in time (false only when fail_on_timeout is off).

prompt_line.description: The line with the prompt, as shown.
